* Experience the classic survival horror formula at its finest, complete with inventory management, optional puzzles, and backtracking to newly unlocked areas and hidden treasures. 
* Use environmental storytelling and scattered clues to solve side mysteries that unlock new outcomes and gameplay bonuses.  
* Thanks to Unreal Engine 5, The Sinking City 2 delivers next-gen visuals with Lumen global illumination, photorealistic Nanite geometry, life-like Metahuman-powered characters, and much more.

games.title: Tukoni: Forest Keepers
games.description: Tukoni: Forest Keepers is a cute & cozy puzzle adventure. Play as Traveller, a forest spirit on a special journey, as you explore magical hand-drawn locations, meet charming characters, solve handcrafted puzzles, collect herbs and tea recipes, and help the forest prepare for the coming winter.

games.title: FEED IT (Games On A Chair)
games.description: A first-person, PSX-style horror game about living with a monster. Do as you're told... or don't. Just be ready for the consequences.

games.title: Lootbound
games.description: Lootbound is a tactical roguelite with turn-based combat, loot management and D&D elements set in a dark fantasy world. Fight dangerous enemies, collect epic loot, recruit allies and lead them on a path of adventure.

games.title: Mafia: The Old Country - Man of Honor
games.description:
Sicily – Winter, 1905. In the months since his initiation, Enzo Favara has proven himself a reliable soldier of the Torrisi crime family. Now the Don entrusts him and Cesare with a delicate assignment: assist Ennio Salieri, a man of honor recently released from prison and intent on reclaiming what is his.

At Salieri's side, Enzo is drawn deeper into the volatile underworld of the Valle Dorata, where loyalty is tested, debts are settled, and every move carries weight.

Continue Enzo's story across two new chapters, featuring fresh environments, weapons, vehicles, and Charms. In new DLC content for Free Ride mode, team up with Salieri to earn big by taking on a new set of exclusive jobs and extreme challenges, and discover new collectibles and hidden locations as you explore.

games.title: Ledgerbound
games.description: Deny an insurance claim, save the world. Ledgerbound is a hilarious, narrative-driven tactical RPG/dating sim filled with all your favorite epic fantasy activities: battling evil enemies, filling out paperwork, rescuing your company from financial ruin, pursuing HR-approved relationships, and more!

games.title: Servant of the Lake
games.description:
Welcome to the Vanderboom house, home to the infamous Vanderboom family! Visitors are arriving soon, and you are meant to start your housekeeping duties immediately!

Solve the puzzles needed to fulfil your daily tasks, look after the household, welcome the visitor and ensure their comfort while helping the family achieve their alchemical ambitions!

Servant of the Lake is the new premium point-and-click adventure in the Rusty Lake series from the creators of the Cube Escape series, The Past Within and Underground Blossom.

games.title: Pro Jank Footy
games.description:
Pro Jank Footy is an absurd and over-the-top arcade sports game.

Score a goal? Your opponent picks a game-changing power-up.

Hinder your opponents, increase your footy abilities with powers that give your team strong legs, or turn the gameplay completely on its head by transforming everyone into footballs - the choice is yours!

Outplay, out-kick, and out-jank your mates in local multiplayer. Or, if you’re shy, conquer single-player season mode.

games.title: EVERSPACE 2: Galactic Edition
games.description:
Experience all of EVERSPACE 2 in one package with the EVERSPACE 2: Galactic Edition. This bundle collects all purchasable EVERSPACE 2 game content into one easy purchase. 

This bundle contains:

- EVERSPACE 2
Experience a 30 hour adventure in this fast-paced single-player spaceship shooter with exploration in space and on planets, tons of loot, RPG elements, mining, and crafting. Explore an exciting sci-fi story set in a vivid, handcrafted open world full of secrets, puzzles, and perils.

- EVERSPACE 2: Titans
The Dreadnought and Leviathan have arrived in Cluster 34. Collect new weapon and gear sets by tackling massive repeatable challenges. Discover two exciting storylines alongside a cast of new and returning characters!

- EVERSPACE 2: Wrath of the Ancients
The Ancients have awakened! Their wrath has laid waste to human settlements in Cluster 34, and the path of destruction leads to the Okkar Homeworlds. Take flight in this massive expansion containing a post-game storyline, exciting side quests, four new star systems, new weapons and gear, and the Wraith starfighter.

games.title: Ghost of Yotei: Complete Edition
games.description: In addition to Echoes of Sekigahara and Most Wanted, this includes the  main Ghost of Yōtei game as well as Ghost of Yōtei Legends, teh online co-op experience with support for up to four players and multiple gameplay modes culminating in a Raid.2 If you purchase the Complete Edition, you can immediately start playing the main game and Legends, and Echoes of Sekigahara and Most Wanted. Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition also includes all of the in-game content previously included in the Ghost of Yōtei Digital Deluxe Edition, as well as the Charm of Hokkyokusei.  [PlayStation]

games.title: Agent 64: Spies Never Die
games.description:
The Agency is sending you on missions all around the world, in order to save it!

Each story mission is a self contained environment where you have to accomplish varied objectives, such as hacking terminals, steal secret plans, free civilian hostages and much more. All the while fighting armed guards in epic shootouts.

Be Agent number 64, the most elite operative the world has ever seen. An absolute legend!

A retro FPS inspired by classic British shooters such as Goldeneye, Perfect Dark and TimeSplitters. Explore new locales, accomplish varied objectives and fight against state-of-the-art 1997 enemy AI.

games.title: IRON NEST: Heavy Turret Simulator
games.description: IRON NEST is a brutal dieselpunk heavy-artillery game where you dominate the battlefield through a colossal war machine. Take map measurements based on the received coordinates, strain the hydraulics, and gunlay the cannons to unleash devastating blows ⟹ Will you obey High Command, Operator?

games.title: Ambrosia Sky: Act Two
games.description:
Act Two completes Dalia’s search for answers behind the crisis engulfing The Cluster and her race to find Maeve. Players can expect resolution to the questions raised in Act One, along with new mission locations, new exo-fungus to harvest and contend with, and an updated progression system featuring new upgrades.

Initially outlined as a three-act arc, the story will conclude with Act Two, allowing Soft Rains to concentrate its full development efforts on delivering a cohesive, polished, and cathartic ending to Dalia’s search for home.

games.title: Sovereign Tower
games.description: Play as the Sovereign of a magical tower in this story-rich, Round Table management RPG. Recruit eccentric Knights, assign quests and balance egos whilst carving out your kingdom's destiny. If destiny doesn’t go your way, keep turning back time, uncover secrets and rewrite fate again and again.

games.title: Obakeidoro 2: Chase & Seek
games.description: OBAKEIDORO 2: Chase & Seek invites players into an eerie world inspired by traditional Japanese legends for a thrilling game of cat-and-mouse. Dive into this monster-infested world solo, or team up with friends! Featuring a unique "scary-cute" character design and charming visuals, this game delivers all the heart-pounding tension of asymmetric multiplayer matches in an accessible, fun package for all ages and horror tolerance levels.

games.title: Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls
games.description: PlayStation Studios, Arc System Works (Arc), and Marvel Games have joined forces to realize the latest in tag team fighters, MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls. Experience the Marvel Universe like never before with reimagined characters and stages, a heart-pounding soundtrack, intuitive gameplay mechanics, and jaw-dropping visuals that promise to keep you on the edge of your seat. Whether this is your first fighting game or you are a veteran of the genre, Arc has incorporated gameplay controls and mechanics that are easy to pick up and play, and yet still offer the depth and versatility for high level competition. Enter the fray with iconic Marvel heroes and villains such as Captain America, Iron Man, Spider-Man, Doctor Doom, Storm, Ms. Marvel, Star-Lord, and Ghost Rider (Robbie Reyes) – each with Arc’s unique twist on their character designs and gameplay styles. [PlayStation]

games.title: Lies of P: Complete Edition
games.description:
The Full Truth Unraveled

The ultimate soulslike experience arrives on Nintendo Switch™ 2. Lies of P: Complete Edition includes the multi-award-winning base game and the Overture expansion, delivering the full saga of Krat’s downfall and the legendary secrets that birthed the Puppet Frenzy.

▶THE DEFINITIVE KRAT CHRONICLE
Explore the full breadth of a world soaked in the style of the Belle Époque. From the blood-stained streets of a collapsed city to the opulent mansions and eerie landmarks of its peak, unearth the complete history of its puppet industry. This edition combines the original narrative with the Overture prequel expansion, offering a comprehensive look at the figures and tragedies that doomed Krat.

▶BATTLE WITH AN EXPRESSIVE ARSENAL
Master a unique combat system of weapon crafting, parrying and gadgetry. Combine the base game’s versatile weapon-making system, mixing blades and handles, with an arsenal of Legion Arms and progression choices for a truly expressive experience. Create devastating combinations to overcome the city's most formidable bosses and twisted mechanical horrors.

▶A SYMPHONY OF CHOICE AND CONSEQUENCE
In a world built on deception, your decisions determine your humanity. Engage with a deepened "Lying System" where choices made in the past ripple through the present. Whether you are comforting a soul in despair or seeking vengeance alongside the Legendary Stalker, every action shapes the narrative, leading to multiple unique endings that define the future of the franchise.

▶OPTIMIZED FOR NINTENDO SWITCH 2
Witness the darkly elegant world of Lies of P in stunning fidelity and performance optimized for the Nintendo Switch 2. This edition includes all post-launch quality-of-life updates, new difficulty modes, new challenge modes, and the seamless integration of the Overture expansion content.

games.title: Montabi
games.description:
Tame, collect, fight! 

Assemble an unstoppable team of unique Montabi in this Creature-Collector Roguelike Deckbuilder. 

Master their awesome abilities, synergize their strategic strengths and save the city in tactical turn-based combat!

games.title: ReStory: Chill Electronics Repairs
games.description:
ReStory is a chill, narrative-driven shop management simulator from the creators of I Am Future, set on the bustling streets of mid-2000s Tokyo and featuring an in-depth device repair system. 

In this game, you run an electronics repair shop, meticulously restore nostalgic Y2K-era devices, including officially licensed Atari consoles, and interact with customers to experience a branching storyline with multiple endings that depend on your choices.

games.title: Doloc Town
games.description: Doloc Town is a cozy pixel-art farming simulation set in a post-apocalyptic world. Build your dream farm from scratch and explore this mysterious wasteland. Harvest, plant, build, and uncover the untold stories of this forgotten land!

games.title: Fields of Mistria
games.description:
Get ready to begin a brand-new life in a world that's brimming with possibilities!

Mistria, an idyllic village tucked between forest and sea, has offered you an overgrown but full-of-potential homestead in exchange for your assistance. Restore the town to its former glory after an earthquake wreaks havoc and strange magic begins to flow through the land.

In this spiritual successor to the Farm-Sim RPGs of the late 90s & onward, build the farm of your dreams as you discover magic, romance, and adventure!

games.title: Pokemon Pokopia: Bubbly Basin
games.description:
Discover Bubbly Basin, a new underwater town, using the move Dive

Use the move Dive—an underwater exploration ability added in a free software update to the Pokémon Pokopia game—to visit the aquatic area of Bubbly Basin in Part 1 of the three-part Pokémon™ Pokopia Expansion Pass DLC*! You’ll find additional furniture items, new outfits for Ditto, and—of course—more Pokémon to meet!

To access Bubbly Basin’s underwater gate, you must first learn Dive and complete the important request “Raise the environment level!” in Bleak Beach.

games.title: Big Walk
games.description:
Big Walk is a cooperative multiplayer adventure about teamwork and talking.

Set out with your friends through a wide-open world full of challenges, puzzles, and discoveries. You'll need to work together to find your way around, stay in contact using an assortment of tools and toys, and figure out new ways to communicate when you suddenly find yourself speechless.

Adventuring aside, there's plenty of time to just hang out. Sit and watch the sunset, or steal your friend's binoculars and kick them into the ocean. Spending time with friends is the best part of a big walk.

games.title: HellSlave II: Judgment of the Archon
games.description:
Thousands of years of demonic warfare have torn the world to shreds. Six demon lords, locked in an endless war, have brought ruin to all. Tired of this infernal chaos, the heavens have unleashed the Archon of Judgment, an unstoppable force set to destroy everything.

But before annihilation can begin, you’re given a final chance at salvation: destroy all the demons yourself or perish with the rest of the world and creation.

Welcome to HellSlave II: Judgment of the Archon, a dark fantasy dungeon crawler RPG where you're humanity's last twisted chance. As the spiritual successor to the critically acclaimed Hellslave, this sequel takes everything fans loved, gritty lore, comic book style hand-drawn art, and tactical combat that raises the bar to hell.

games.title: PAW Patrol: Dino World
games.description:
ROARR! Sounds like trouble… Did that come from Dino Island? 
Mayor Humdinger is causing chaos, making the dinosaurs scared and run away.  

Leap into colossal rescue missions with Chase, Marshall, Rubble, Skye, Rocky, and Zuma. Explore the Dino Plains and care for dinos at the Paleo Center. Drive across the shores and jungle to discover collectibles.  

Create roar-some new looks for your pup, vehicle, and dinosaurs. Play fun minigames in solo or in two-player mode.  

Can you stop the chaos before the volcano erupts? No dino’s too big, no pup’s too small in this prehistoric adventure!

games.title: Truxton Extreme
games.description:
Get ready for Truxton Extreme - a new action-pumped shoot 'em up from Tatsujin!

Truxton Extreme, which inherits the DNA from legendary arcade masterpiece Truxton, is a collaboration with manga artist and Toaplan alumni Junya Inoue, and bursts onto PlayStation 5 next year!

games.title: Xenoblade Chronicles 2: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition
games.description:
Lead Rex, Pyra, and the world to refuge in an adventure enhanced for the Nintendo Switch™ 2 system!

Lost in a sea of clouds, entire civilizations rest on the backs of Titans. As the giant beasts march toward death, the last hope is a scavenger named Rex—and Pyra, a living weapon known as a Blade. Command a group of Blades and lead them to countless strategic victories as you search for the fabled paradise Pyra calls home. This journey has been enhanced with 4K* resolution in TV mode, and full HD in handheld mode, at 60 frames per second—and with smoother and sharper cutscenes.

Discover a new rare Blade—and control your Blades to fight in mercenary squad battles

Not only is there an additional Blade out there for you to find—along with a quest to complete—but you can directly command your Blades in a new action battle mode!

Unlock new equipment designs for Pyra and Mythra

Customize the look of Pyra and Mythra with new equipment designs exclusive to this Nintendo Switch 2 Edition game.

Already have Xenoblade Chronicles™ 2 for Nintendo Switch? Purchase the upgrade pack!

games.title: Midnight Moments
games.description: A small, cyberpunk diorama-building game where you create cozy rain-soaked backstreets, glowing apartment blocks, or quiet neighbourhood corners. Decorate your designs with props and place citizens. At your own pace. No goals. Just vibes.

games.title: Blue Reflection Quartet
games.description:
The BLUE REFLECTION series depicts the emotions and bonds of teenage girls across a variety of mediums, with character design and series supervision by famed illustrator Mel Kishida. BLUE REFLECTION Quartet contains all four of these emotional stories in a single collection.

New features make the series more accessible than ever before, with a more detailed look at the setting that will help newcomers understand events and provide a deeper look for returning fans.

BLUE REFLECTION
A console game which told the story of an injured former ballerina as she used her powers as a magical Reflector to form bonds with others and fight off the looming threat to the world. Textures have been updated to high resolution versions, and new visual effects such as glistening water add to the world's atmosphere. New features such as autosave have been included, offering a more enjoyable experience than ever before.

BLUE REFLECTION: RAY
An anime that tells the story of magical Reflectors clashing with each other over their conflicting beliefs and emotions.
This game tells a condensed version of the story, with the major characters rendered in 3D.
Follow Hiori and Ruka as they explore the Common while re-experiencing their memories on their way to confront a girl trying to recreate the world. New short stories expand on the anime's story, and a new prologue and epilogue connect this entry to the other works in the series.

BLUE REFLECTION: SUN
A mobile game that told the story of a team of girls living in a dying world as they hold on to hope for the future.
SUN's story has been remade as a console game using the systems of BLUE REFLECTION: Second Light to recreate the memorable battles of the original game. 24 new character events have been added alongside the main story, and the prologue and epilogue from the original release connect this entry to the other works in the series.

BLUE REFLECTION: Second Light
A console game that tells the story of a group of girls with no memories who find themselves in a strange world. Through their adventures, the girls must look deep inside their hearts, regain their memories, and discover the truth about the world they are living in.
This entry in the BLUE REFLECTION project first came out in October of 2021. This release for BLUE REFLECTION Quartet features eight additional characters from RAY and SUN who can join you in battle. These new characters also join Yuzuki and Lime as new additions to the Photo Mode! New features such as increased battle speed, faster movement speed while exploring, and event fast-forwarding have been included, offering a more enjoyable experience than ever before.

games.title: Jotunnslayer: Hordes of Hel
games.description:
Jotunnslayer: Hordes of Hel is a gripping roguelike horde arena survival game with top-notch graphics. Choose one of the damned heroes and attempt to pass the gods' test by fighting your way through waves of mythical adversaries.

If you succeed in all the trials, you will become the chosen Jotunnslayer.

Engage in adrenaline-fueled battles, fighting off endless waves of enemies as you strive to survive. Complete various objectives, defeat the final boss, and earn the ultimate prizes.

games.title: Rita
games.description: Rita is a cozy adventure where a little chicklet solves word-based puzzles to transform the world around her. Follow her story across generations, meet her grandchicklet, and be a part of her legacy.

games.title: SENARA: The Sacrament
games.description: A claustrophobic ocean liner, relentless cultists, and horrific monstrosities. Inspired by classic survival horror like Resident Evil, gather clues, solve puzzles, and uncover the truth. Where fanaticism and salvation collide, you must make choices beyond mere survival.

games.title: Kusan: City of Wolves
games.description:
Kusan: City of Wolves is a hardcore top-down shooter set in the bloody Port City of the Asia in the near future. 

You are a former soldier turned back-alley fixer, tasked with protecting a girl who possesses the power to endanger the city. With your military-grade combat prosthetic 'War Hand', the auto-targeting 'Quantum Knife', and your weapon of choice, eliminate enemies and safeguard the girl. Stand against the plan of your fallen comrade and crush his corrupted will. You are faster and stronger than any beast.

Protect the girl against the coup plan of an old comrades. Be an expert in combat skills, prosthetics, guns and knife. The fiercest beast in the city, you are.

games.title: Halo: Campaign Evolved
games.description:
Halo: Campaign Evolved is a faithful yet modernized remake of Halo: Combat Evolved’s campaign. Experience the original story rebuilt with high-definition visuals, updated cinematics, and refined controls, plus three brand-new prequel missions featuring the Master Chief and Sgt. Johnson. 

A broader arsenal of weapons, vehicles, enemies, and gameplay-modifying "Skulls" - optional modifiers that change combat in fun and challenging ways - add fresh tactics and endless replayability.

Play it your way: solo or up to 4-player online co-op with full crossplay and cross-progression support. 

Whether you’re discovering Halo for the first time or returning to the ring after 25 years, Halo: Campaign Evolved delivers an adventure that feels both timeless and brand new.

games.title: Shards of Order
games.description: A grim RPG with card-based combat where nothing stays dead. Lead a party of survivors through a world undone by shattered Laws. Restore them and reshape the rules of the game, but be ready to face the consequences.

games.title: Lunarium
games.description: Lunarium is an atmospheric fantasy A-RPG. Play as Ave, a light-armored knight, who teams up with Lune, a mysterious Starfarer. Together, they journey to save a dying world, engaging in challenging battles to retrieve the lost glow of the stars and forsaken memories, unveiling cosmic secrets.

games.title: Tormentum II
games.description:
Tormentum II is a Point & Click adventure game taking place in a dark, surreal world full of gloomy characters and repulsive creatures taken straight from the scariest horrors. The hand-drawn graphics, referring to the work of outstanding painters such as H.R.Giger or Zdzisaw Beksiski, will take care of the one-of-a-kind impressions that spice up the players with shivers.

This time the adventure will begin in the future -- in a universe where computer games bring relief in a hopeless world devastated by technology. Players will lead the fate of a game creator whose ambition is to create what has never been achieved before -- a world inhabited by characters with intelligence equal to that of a human being.

When one day he receives a mysterious package with a strange processor, worrying visions begin to haunt him. Reality mixes with a nightmare, and characters from the game begin to penetrate his world. Or maybe it's the other way round...

He decides to place a mysterious processor in his computer. From that moment nothing is certain anymore, and he himself becomes a prisoner of his own creation. He wakes up in prison on an island in the middle of the sea and starts exploring the world he has created. However, he turns out to be different from his imagination -- much less friendly, much more aggressive. However, one thing puzzles him the most: the characters he encounters tell him about a god who lives on one of the most remote islands. About a god who has never been in his game, which he himself has not created.

Players will be able to get to know the huge dark world stretching to several islands. Full of secrets and rich in various creatures. In order to find his way home and find a mysterious god along the way, the protagonist will have to travel through a vast land, which will consist of more than 130 locations -- twice as many as in the first part of the adventure.

games.title: Gurei
games.description: Gurei is a highly-challenging action game created by Lobo Sagaz Studio. Drawing inspiration from classic Japanese samurai films (“chanbara”), Gurei features a gorgeous hand-drawn art style with fluid animations. With its carefully-designed combat system, a wealth of attack moves obtainable throughout the gameplay, and snappy, responsive controls, players are guaranteed to enjoy the satisfying action gameplay experience that Gurei offers.

games.title: Helix: Descent N Ascent
games.description:
Embark in Helix, an adventure into the depths of a forgotten world. Progress in a nonlinear fashion, combining your powers to solve puzzles and unveil secrets. Dive into a visually captivating and immersive tale that tests your wit and cloaks you with its atmospheric soundtrack.

Awakening in a world of contrasts, you set off to discover it. Embark on a cryptic adventure, unearth secrets, investigate the fate of a lost civilization, collect artifacts, and respond to the haunting call that beckons. 

This is a tale interwoven with threads of melancholy and the undying spirit of the past.

games.title: High Times
games.description:
In a world where you can literally eat your feelings, you work at The Hotbox, a one-of-a-kind donut shop where every donut is infused with mood enhancers that can change your customers’ emotions. But people don’t always know what they need, so from flavors that give them courage to ones that lift their spirits, it’s up to you to choose the right mood and help each troubled customer. Listen to their stories, offer advice in the form of donuts, and help mend broken relationships.

FEATURES

games.title: Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game
games.description:
Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game is a fast-paced 1v1 fighter where you battle as your favorite characters from the Avatar franchise. Featuring hand-drawn 2D animation true to the series’ roots, proprietary rollback netcode, and full cross-play for smooth, competitive gameplay.

Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game is a fighter rooted in the spirit of elemental mastery. Designed for both newcomers and veterans, it channels the energy of classic fighting games while breaking new ground in movement, style, and combat expression. Built with a focus on fluidity, responsiveness, and online integrity, the game invites players to discover what it truly means to fight with purpose.

Hand-drawn in 2D, it is crafted to preserve the style and expressive animation of the original series.

games.title: Dodo Duckie!
games.description:
You’re a DUCK! with one special cap that gives you the power to switch between 2D and 3D. 

Use it to explore, switch perspectives, solve puzzles and save your chicken friends.

games.title: Dinoblade
games.description: Dinoblade is an intense action RPG set in a prehistoric world forever changed by a cataclysmic event. Step into the role of a young Spinosaurus, wielding a colossal Great Sword. Confront rival dinosaurs, some armed with weapons of their own, all in a desperate fight to prevent a looming extinction.

games.title: CULTIC
games.description: Death is only the beginning. Crawl from your grave and gear up to fight your way through the ranks of a mysterious and twisted cult. You, your guns, and your dynamite will have to shoot, slide, blast, duck, dodge, and maybe throw a gib or two to survive in this old-school-inspired shooter.

games.title: Splatoon Raiders
games.description: Play as the 'Mechanic' and explore the mysterious Spirhalite Islands alongside Deep Cut in Splatoon Raiders, a new Splatoon spin-off game launching exclusively for Nintendo Switch 2.

games.title: DragonSword : Awakening
games.description: Explore the anime-style open world of the Continent of Orbis, brought to life with Unreal Engine 5! Recruit unique companions, unleash spectacular Status Ailment tag-team action, and embark on an epic journey to save the world from the threat of a Dragon reawakened after 60 years.

games.title: Rubinite
games.description: In this dark fantasy boss rush, use Ruby's crimson eyes to expose the weak points of the Bloodstained monsters, then strike and shatter them. Carve a road home through the ruined Scarlet Kingdom and face the Witch who took it all.

games.title: Staffer Retro: A Supernatural Mystery Quest
games.description: Staffer Retro is a mystery adventure game where you uncover past incidents related to ‘Mana’, the source of supernatural powers. Gather information through dialogue and exploration, and piece together clues found in documents to guide the choices of Verita Retro, the protagonist.

games.title: Nightmare Frontier
games.description:
Behold the first-ever Tactical Extraction Looter where you pit your courage and leadership against fears made manifest: the Dreadweavers.

Lead a band of scavenger roughnecks into a devastated boom town of the alternative 1900s. 

Get in, face the monsters, grab what you can carry and get out. Alive.

games.title: DIVE or DIE - Children of Rain
games.description:
Explore the Abyssal Pool, an underwater labyrinth of drowned ruins, lost idols, and mutated monsters. Lead a band of desperate survivors with Jack, a haunted man with a singular purpose: to save what's left of humanity.

Evade or fight what lurks in the dark. And try to appease the Maker of Rain before he floods the world in his black tears.

games.title: Fading Echo
games.description:
Explore the surreal landscapes of the floating islands of Corel as a young Legend on a quest to discover her past and secure her future. Unleash chain reactions as you learn to control the elements in a fast-paced desert punk action-adventure. 

Use water as a weapon in all its forms. Seamlessly transform between liquid and human forms to navigate Corel’s surreal landscapes and battle its dangers. Dissolve into a droplet to slip through cracks and spread water across your surroundings, surge through tubes, crash down as a water bomb, or ascend in a vapor burst. 

Traverse Corel and its Shadows, distorted realities of the same world, each with its own laws, dangers, and possibilities. Explore landscapes both familiar and alien to unlock precious Aetheric Sources, discover new ways to interact with the world and adapt your approach to each dimension.

reviews.quote: Just Dance: Decades of Hits is a wonderfully entertaining game, and the only thing more fun than playing it is watching someone else dance

A Just Dance that changes its name more than its formula. While the new Adventure Mode adds little to the experience, the game is still the perfect excuse to get everyone off the couch and onto the dance floor.

Just Dance: Decades of Hits works where it matters. At the end of the day it’s a fun workout game that allows for a lot of flexibility when it comes to the song choice. It has an annoying but ultimately unobtrusive way of asking you to spend more money, but if you find the main game is worth it, who's to say the extras aren’t worth it to you, too?

Battleplan is the first game that makes me feel like I was playing RISK as a kid with adults who knew much better than me. Generally speaking, strategy games either give you full tactical control or go grand and make you handle taxation on wood imports from your neighbor. Battleplan strikes a balance by giving you an intimate view of the action but from the general's chair. The realistic depiction of historical engagements is a treat, with mechanics that never go deeper than they have to in order to deliver unforgettable emergent narratives. As it is, Battleplan is a great game, and some quality-of-life additions to the interface are all that's left from making it the perfect strategy title.

Battleplan does something intriguing by mixing a highly detailed real-time strategy experience based on World War II with relatively limited player control over the action. Planning via drawing is accessible and fast, and the game encourages players to try out strategies and replay battles. The OOB and officer upgrade system is very good. The presentation is decent, although zooming in to see how units actually do battle isn’t advised, and there’s plenty of attention to detail in the battle setup and briefings. Battleplan is a good game for anyone who feels intimidated by the complexity of most military strategy but might be too hands-off for some hardcore genre fans.

Alpha Nomos can be a little repetitive at times, and it can feel as though there isn’t an abundance of content to unlock, but it still remains a fairly fun and distinctly creative experience throughout. The game’s unique mix of rhythm-game mechanics and roguelike progression, paired with its fun story and characters, makes for an undeniably memorable experience.

Colorbound is a small yet great and colourful journey all about life and its inevitable end. With a gripping soundtrack, tricky puzzles, and just seeing the sheer amount of love on display, this is highly recommended.
Burn With Me is a dreadfully cosy little game where forethought and planning will get you through with sanity intact.

Just like protagonist Alan alternates between two versions of his mind's reality, Time To Wake Up alternates between being an underwhelming and a brilliant one. While the Belgian Eye Blink Twice holds two very interesting cards - being an important story regarding depression and an clever core mechanic of blinking to swap the scenery - it doesn't seem to feel comfortable playing any of them with conviction throughout the full two hours. There's something beautiful to be found in Time To Wake Up, but it takes a couple of blinks to really see it.

reviews.author: LL2Heaven
reviews.quote:
I believe this game is named to intentionally mislead people interested in the PC game “Wind Rose” or the RPG “Broken Compass” into accidentally purchasing their unity slop game.

Graphically the game is ugly.  Bland textures, low poly count, almost zero foliage that pops in only at very close distances.  The water is not animated and just a blue plane that clips through the ship.  I also found myself constantly clipping through objects that appeared to be solid.

Gameplay is extremely simple.  You can board the ship where your view is fixed straight ahead and can fire from a set of left and right cannons.  None of this is animated so all you see when you press the button is the icon darkened for a few seconds.  Additionally water is instant death and you’ll clip thought the railing of your ship right into the water.  

Land combat involves simply punching.  No swords, no pistols, just fists.  The response feels sluggish and the enemies shrink away to nothing when killed.  They don’t drop any loot and there’s no experience to gain so the only reason to bother attacking them at all is to keep them from killing you.

You can collect treasure chests but they’re just randomly placed out in the open where you hit a button and the game just tells you how much gold you got.  However there’s nothing to spend your gold on so it’s just there like a score card.

Ultimately this game is a zero effort cash grab hoping to exploit customers who believe they’re buying something else.

Hidden cat games have a tendency to release new iterations every couple of months, and if Hidden Dogs followed that pattern then I would be first in line. If it was a dog, it would be a labrador: not particularly revolutionary or unfamiliar, but so endearing and good-natured, with a couple of tricks in its repertoire, that you can’t help falling in love with it.

Truckful offers a relaxing yet occasionally tense driving experience, combining package deliveries with a mysterious story, side missions, and collectibles. Its engaging narrative and puzzle-based gameplay make exploring enjoyable, although judging the depth of the environment can sometimes be difficult. Despite some grindy Scrap collecting, Truckful delivers a unique and compact adventure.

Truckful is a strange delivery game that shines in its genre mix, blending horror with cozy exploration. However, it also has plenty of speed bumps in its controls and exploration, creating a frustrating driving experience that could use more quality-of-life improvements. Still, once you get past those roadblocks, the game becomes surprisingly heartfelt, with a compelling story and a charming cast of NPCs who stick with you as you unravel the town's mysteries. It’s a bumpy ride, but if you’re willing to stick with it, Truckful is worth taking for a spin.

Truckful‘s flow might be interrupted by frequent loading screens, but it is otherwise a pretty fun, relaxing physics-puzzle about driving through a beautiful countryside delivering packages. That is, until sudden, unexpected but much-appreciated horror elements show up, giving the game a unique and threatening element not present in similar titles.

Truckful has a surprisingly deep, dark story with a lot of enjoyable, entertaining characters. This carried me through the game more than I expected, and I’m glad I got to experience what it had to offer. The physics are hit or miss depending on your driving, but the core mechanics and handling are fun. The game excels in story, world-building, mystery, and, more often than not, the main gameplay loop.

In the long run—much like any video game that simulates a job—Truckful turns into a routine: you end up doing the same things and, for the most part, driving the same roads. You move from one character to another, sometimes just to update them on the situation before speeding off to the next conversation. Car chases become few and far between—save for the showdown with the two ghosts—and the entire cargo-hauling mechanic tends to become monotonous. Ultimately, Truckful is a hard game to pin down: it aims to be "cozy" but fails, as the driving mechanics and camera angles will only frustrate you. It tries to be a thriller, yet that element becomes increasingly muted. It sets out to be a job-simulation game but embraces only the worst possible aspect of the job: the routine. The same faces, the same roads, the same packages—over and over again. At a certain point, you’ll even grow tired of the trees, the tree-lined roads, and the little birds.

An unexpected gem in almost every way. I don't think many were crying out for a Hellraiser game, but everyone will be demanding a sequel to Revival, as Saber's horror show delivers a compelling, rich journey through pain and pleasure.

Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival is a fantastic game that’ll satisfy both franchise and horror survival fans. Depending on whether or not you can stomach it, of course. It really doesn’t hold back, as it shouldn’t. Between the intense cinematics and the gut-wrenching narrative, this game pulls on every string. The Cenobites of Clive Barker’s world are known for two things: pain and pleasure. And this game showcases it all. There were many times when, while adventuring through the cultists’ underground lair, the world at large, or through the sex club, I had to scrape my jaw off the floor. It is a spectacle, and if you can handle a metric ton of body horror, this game should be on your radar.

Hellraiser: Revival is a faithful adaptation of the universe created by Clive Barker, combining an oppressive atmosphere, grotesque visuals, and genuinely tense moments with a structure heavily inspired by games of the genre, most notably Resident Evil 4 Remake. Although the puzzles are simple and the difficulty decreases considerably as the player masters its mechanics and abilities, the campaign manages to hold its own thanks to the excellent setting, intense chases, and creative use of the Lament Configuration. It's not revolutionary, but it's an interesting and authentic survival horror game for fans of the genre and, especially, of Hellraiser.

Those unfamiliar with Barker’s work who are looking for a strong title in this genre will find one that offers plenty of variety and a striking visual identity. It may not reinvent the wheel, but it knows how to combine its gameplay elements in a highly effective and engaging way.
Hellraiser: Revival is at its best when its horror gamification takes a back seat, providing a world that is equal parts depraved and disturbing, scary and thrilling.
Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival is not for those with weak stomachs. It's also got a lot of painful imagery. If you can power through that, there's a solid survival horror experience underneath.

I am pleasantly surprised at how much I enjoyed Hellraiser: Revival. Its respect for its source material is apparent throughout, with the Labyrinth, the Cenobites, and the Genesis Configuration being standout pieces of the puzzle. The rest of the game isn't reinventing the wheel for first-person horror, but the "don't fix what isn't broken" approach works just fine here. The squeamish need not apply, as there are moments made to make your skin crawl, but even the most horror-averse people can have a great time in this Labyrinth. Saber Interactive has such sights to show you, and thankfully, there's more pleasure than pain.

Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival delivers an excellent adaptation by expanding the franchise's mythology and book lore, bringing back the classic voice of Pinhead alongside a bold Unreal Engine 5 art direction. Although it stumbles confusedly between deliberate survival horror and action FPS, the title establishes itself as a worthy adaptation of the series' cultural impact.

Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival succeeds above all where it matters most: atmosphere, visual identity, and fidelity to the franchise’s aesthetic. The Genesis Configuration adds personality to a fairly traditional survival horror framework, though issues with balancing, AI, and protagonist writing hold back its potential. A successful adaptation, even if not without its rough edges.

It has some issues than can annoy, such as difficulty spikes and a couple of troublesome forced stealth sections, but these don't stop Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival from being a thrilling rollercoaster of a survival horror experience. Sexy, gory and grotesque are perhaps the best words to sum it up.

reviews.author: lionelhut
reviews.quote: Hellraiser: Revival me ha parecido un juego sobresaliente, especialmente teniendo en cuenta que no es una producción triple A en sentido estricto. Su jugabilidad es muy divertida y recuerda claramente a Resident Evil Village: dispone de varias armas mejorables, munición siempre escasa y un inventario limitado que obliga a organizar los objetos como si fuera un pequeño **** sistema de mejoras de armas resulta algo incompleto. Como no se pueden instalar todas simultáneamente, al final las opciones más útiles suelen ser las que aumentan el daño y la capacidad de munición, dejando el resto en un segundo plano.Tanto los enemigos normales como los jefes presentan un diseño excelente y ofrecen enfrentamientos variados. La escasez de balas mantiene la tensión durante toda la aventura, mientras que la gestión del inventario añade una capa estratégica bastante **** ambientación es, sin duda, uno de sus mayores logros. Los escenarios, la música y el diseño de sonido crean una atmósfera brutal. El Laberinto de Leviatán transmite realmente la sensación de estar atrapado en otro mundo, oscuro, opresivo y con un terror cercano a lo lovecraftiano. El misterio que rodea a los personajes, los cenobitas y los acontecimientos también está muy bien **** trabajo de voces está a gran nivel, destacando especialmente Doug Bradley como Pinhead, cuya interpretación es uno de los mejores elementos del **** historia es muy buena y cuenta con un guion bastante sólido. Mi principal crítica es que numerosos personajes advierten al protagonista de que ayudar a Sunny podría ser un error, pero él continúa haciéndolo sin cuestionarse seriamente sus intenciones. Esa falta de dudas hace que su comportamiento resulte algo forzado en determinados momentos.Gráficamente alcanza un nivel notable. Los modelados de los personajes son discretos, pero cumplen correctamente. Su verdadera fortaleza está en los escenarios, la dirección artística y la recreación del universo de Hellraiser. Además, es un juego claramente dirigido a un público adulto, con escenas muy fuertes, violencia explícita y un tono **** conjunto, es un survival horror muy recomendable, con una jugabilidad entretenida, excelentes enemigos, buena historia y una ambientación extraordinaria. Sus limitaciones en las mejoras de armas y algunas decisiones cuestionables del protagonista no impiden que sea una experiencia sobresaliente. Una de las sorpresas del 2026

reviews.author: Clappy07
reviews.quote:
When I first heard they were making a Hellraiser game I expected one of those multiplayer dead by daylight kind of clone games that all the other horror movie franchises have hopped on. 

Then I heard its a single player story driven game, this perked my interest but I thought there's no way they could make a story which feels like it fits in the hellraiser universe, particularly with its overly sexual themes etc. I was expecting something watered down.

I was wrong... as a lifelong Hellraiser fan this game feels absolutely perfect in pretty much every way. It massively exceeded my expectations. The story works, the locations and themes fit with particularly the first two movies. 

I think non hellraiser fans might not like it as it doesn't do anything groundbreaking as a horror game and there isn't much replay value but for any fan of the movies this is a must play Its probably my favourite horror game so far this year!

It's also an absolute bargain price too! half the price of most AAA games and its in fact a lot better than a few of them.

The game feels like a 90s B-horror movie, while the gameplay is reminiscent of games from the 2000s. The shooting and melee feel a bit clunky, stealth feels a bit clunky, crafting and item management feel clunky, and the story is just interesting enough to hold your attention. The gameplay and puzzles feel like a sort of Resident Evil Light. But my goodness, what a great atmosphere! If you're a fan of horror movies like Hellraiser, then this game is for you. The developers clearly watched the first two films; this could easily have been a sequel written by Clive Barker himself. The artwork is a mix of M.C. Escher and Hell itself. The music is incredibly atmospheric, and the graphics are solid thanks to that outstanding art direction.

​The game is far from perfect, but the same went for Clive Barker's Hellraiser—and yet that’s a movie I love, which is exactly how I feel about this game.
Fantastic budget survival Horror game, for a reasonable budget price.

over the hill is a game that makes you fall in love with it. It challenges you without passing judgment. It gives you freedom while still guiding you through the desire to upgrade your car, and it rewards you whenever you discover something interesting on the map. Above all, Over the Hill is a game brimming with a love for the automotive world—a passion infused into every single polygon.

Over the Hill builds on Art of Rally’s tactile driving and distils the appeal of Saber Interactive’s complex off-roading sims into something much more approachable. The cute animal photography is the cherry on top.

over the hill is a peaceful sandbox game that gives you the freedom to do whatever you want to do. You can play with friends, roam the sandbox together while checking off objectives, or just enjoy your time in the cozy world. Playing alone can make the world feel a bit empty; it still has some kinks to work out, but there’s a very good time to be had just driving around and listening to the radio while you watch the sunset from a peak you just climbed.

The game's performance has been good; while it ran smoothly almost the entire time during our tests on a high-end rig, we do not expect it to perform as well on low-end PCs, given its significant RAM usage.

A few quality-of-life issues could use some work, but otherwise, over the hill reaffirms Funselektor’s knack for creating unusual and engaging driving experiences. Off-roading through the mountains isn’t for everyone, yet the Canadian studio’s latest manages to be accessible to newcomers, offering co-op sessions that can go on for hours without a hitch. If trekking through picturesque landscapes sounds appealing, over the hill will welcome you with open arms.

Ultimately, Over the Hill is a lovely little adventure that understands the simple joy of heading out into the wilderness and seeing what you stumble across. For me, it’s at its best when you’re tackling its trickier trails with friends, where a seemingly straightforward expedition can quickly descend into a chaotic and often hilarious rescue mission where you’ll be eating popcorn by the bucket-load. Progression could do with a little fine-tuning, and I personally don’t find solo play to have quite have the same appeal as multiplayer, but regardless – there’s a lot to like here. If you like the idea of going it alone, or if you’ve got a few friends willing to pile into their 4x4s and head up the trail with you, Over the Hill is well worth the trip.

over the hill offers a fun, easy-going offroading experience. But while I had a good time tackling the terrain both solo and with friends, there’s not a lot to do besides in the beautiful but barren environments. Future updates and DLC may eventually breathe more life into it, but until then over the hill remains a very casual experience that’ll only keep you occupied for brief stints.

While some players may find plenty of enjoyment in over the hill, its multiplayer adds little to the experience. The game looks peaceful, its simplistic art style is charming and the soundtrack fits the intended atmosphere, but frustrating exploration and underwhelming rewards quickly ruin that sense of tranquillity. Bumper Christmas lights are pretty funny, but not when you’ve tumbled down a hill thirty-seven times just to get them.

Almost the anti-driving game. Over The Hill is slow, laborious, and frequently frustrating. The vast game areas are adequately detailed yet oddly empty-feeling. While the expertly curated trial routes are standouts, you're essentially perpetually playing the worst bits of every open world driving game again and again, with little sense of variety or reward.

It's a game gloriously devoid of feature creep or noise, of time limits or competition: a refreshing, head-clearing space. In its quietly rugged way, it's the perfect cozy game. You watch your valiant little 4x4 crawl and bounce across a luscious wilderness as the sun rises and ambient guitar music wafts through the speakers and feel your heart fill with a kind of entranced patience. There's no rush. You'll get there in the end.

Balancing Lunne’s business, relationships, and magical growth as a Heart Witch was one of the best gaming experiences I’ve had all year. With each passing in-game day, I fell more in love with the world and everyone in it. Now, I only want more players to experience the same joy I’ve had with The Witch’s Bakery, so do not let this one go overlooked.

Ultimately, Thank You, Bus Driver is not a full-fledged game in any traditional sense or price. What it actually is may be more important for them right now; an assertion of the passion and creativity that Double Fine have as a developer, no matter what the budget or timeframe. A few hours of chaotic fun delivered with signature charm; it’s more of an entertaining curio than anything else. Even so, it is small, but worthy addition to the Double Fine catalogue for fans of the studio and hopefully – a good sign of things to come.

Thank You Bus Driver delivers a quirky, charming spin on arcade driving with satisfying bus handling, chaotic passenger management, and an inventive 1950s cartoon aesthetic. Its roguelite progression and shifting rules create some entertaining runs, but limited variety, repetitive objectives, and an irritating soundtrack cause the novelty to wear thin long before the journey is over.

Shockwave Triggers is an old-school shooter that is addictive. I love the cooperative approach, the different enemies, and the basic ideas. Despite the lack of depth, I enjoyed the fast-paced and often eye-watering action.

The hypnotic, amphetamine joys of rampaging through cities as a meatball big enough to satisfy god don't last out the whole game, and what Rolla asked of me to see its final levels was  beyond both my skill and patience. But Rolla still executes its simple concept with brilliantly evil flair. There's no fat on this awful meat sphere.

Hungry Horrors, from developer Clumsy Bear Studio, is a card-based joy to play. It’s engaging, wonderfully circular in its design, and an easy game to revisit regularly. The difficulty might turn some gamers away, but once that hill is climbed, it’s a brilliantly built game that will be tough to put down.

The Early Access version of Hungry Horrors is a pretty great introduction to what can be both a unique and incredibly fun title, one that mixes up its own genre with unique mechanics and shows off some very fun character writing and creature designs. I highly recommend this game, even in Early Access, and can’t wait to see what comes with the full release. [Early Access Review]

Deep Dish Dungeon is a fun, quirky little expedition that offers challenging combat and fun food crafting, set in a retro dark fantasy world. Crafting feels immediate and enjoyable, and though the combat may not work for everyone, but if you grew up playing King's Field, it will feel like stepping into a portal to the past.

Deep Dish Dungeon is a game of its time. It taps into the trend of cooperative survival games, successfully connecting with the genre while offering a nostalgic touch by adopting an aesthetic reminiscent of games from bygone eras.

Mortal Shell 2 is not only one of the best soulslikes ever released, but it also has the potential to spark small revolutions within the genre. The "shell" mechanic — which allows you to experiment with distinct classes throughout the game — is not only fun but also crucial for devising strategies during the campaign. The same applies to the associated abilities and subtle tweaks to traditional combat, such as the absence of a stamina bar.

Mortal Shell 2 is such an immensely impressive upgrade from the original that I wanted it to be flawless. Of course, it isn't. However, issues with pacing, opacity, occasional difficulty spikes, and bugs are dwarfed by Cold Symmetry's overall achievement. If Mortal Shell was a short story, Mortal Shell 2 is a richly textured epic novel. The Shell System has been fully realized. The shift from stamina to Resolve pushes combat towards relentless action and risk. If Mortal Shell was an appetizer, Mortal Shell 2 is a full, satisfying meal and should be in the library of every Soulslike fan.
Currently sitting in my top five releases of the year, fans of gritty Soulslike action RPGs will absolutely love Mortal Shell II.

Any fan of the Souls-like genre needs to experience Mortal Shell II. The difference from the first game to the second is substantial, offering a visual experience that’s beautiful and well-optimized. It showcases what Unreal Engine 5 can do and provides a world of both dark morbidity and beautiful greenery.
Cold Symmetry's expansive Mortal Shell 2 is a true soulslike gem, offering terrific build variety and a beautiful world that rewards exploration.

Mortal Shell 2 seems to be built for those who enjoyed the oppressive atmosphere and brutal combat of the first game but longed for greater depth. It retains the weight of the combat, the enigmatic narrative, and the punishing philosophy typical of the series, while expanding progression, situational variety, and freedom of action. It doesn't simply try to imitate Dark Souls or Elden Ring: it takes many ideas from classic Souls-like games, but continues to forge its own identity based on the harshness of the combat, the strategic use of Shells, and a world that feels more alive and independent than its predecessor. Let's sum it all up: do you like Souls? Buy it.
To call Mortal Shell 2 an improvement over the first game feels like underselling it. It's bigger, tighter, deeper, wider.

Mortal Shell 2 is a fantastic soulslike that felt rewarding to play through and experiment with. The way the progression systems work encourages trying new ways to play, and I can feel the differences as we continually try new things and get stronger. The story is easier to follow than others in the genre, and the world is creepy and beautiful. Some of the camera angles can be a little obnoxious, but at the end of the day, this is one of the best soulslikes out there.

Mortal Shell II takes everything that worked in the original and turns it into a much stronger, more confident Soulslike. The deeper Shell system, satisfying combat, and rewarding exploration stand out, and despite the camera issues and some frustrating progression choices, none of those issues stopped me from having a damn good time with it. This is a fantastic follow-up and Cold Symmetry has seated themselves at the big table with Mortal Shell II.
Cold Symmetry has built a game that is extraordinarily close to a perfect center of difficulty for me with a clear north star of “make it fun, first.”

Ama oyunun asıl eksi yediği yer teknik taraflar. 30. saatte bütün save dosyam silindi. Ana menüde yeni oyun yazıyordu sadece. Yedeklerle falan bir şekilde 2 saat önceki save'e döndüm ama aklım gitti. Ayrıca sık sık çöküyor. Hızlı seyahatlerde gidebiliyor. Birkaç defa boss kestiğim anda, feneri temizleyip başa dönme ekranında falan gitti. Açılışta 30 fps'ye kilitlemek gerekiyor, yoksa harita yüklenirken çöküyor. Yüklenince yeniden fps kilidini yükseltebiliyorsunuz ama yukarıda dedğim gibi çökme ihtimali hep var. Tüm bu aksiliklere rağmen oynamaya devam ettim çünkü iyi bir oyun. Ama deneyimim baltalandı, yalan yok.

Nihayetinde oynadığım en iyi soulslike'lardan birisi. Özellikle atmosfer, evren ve harita tasarımı ile.

My bow stayed +5 my whole playthrough; the axe-shooter is only +6. Grinding this hard near the end is bad. It would encourage experimentation if you were not locked **** a fan of self adjusting difficulty and night mode. They feel like crutches to fix an unbalanced game. Mommons is clearly later.I am a 70% player who never farmed or leveled intentionally, just explored and did the one night thing in the Mushroom Village chapel; levels came in too fast, making bosses trivial.Only maxing out two shells per playthrough discourages experimentation, and I must refund and re-level shells every switch. Just give each shell the same pool of points. Stupid **** hub area is generic and boring. It never feels like home or moody, just annoying running 100 meters to each NPC.NPCs say the same dull dialogue, no quests that I found. Only the tunnel guy and the "commune with chaos" entrance revealed **** music ****, not because it is bad but because about 3 tracks loop endlessly everywhere. I had to turn it off, though the ambient dungeon sounds are a good mix. Same gloomy track all the time.Boss music is ridiculous "background metal", as toned down as the world, even more. Compare to the Doom 2016 soundtrack. A joke: not proper boss music, only 3 tracks for the **** constantly get stuck in the environment after dodging or being knocked into the level. reviews.author: Testarudo
reviews.quote: Un soulslike que aporta sus propias ideas y personalidad al género. El primer Mortal Shell era un juego modesto, con evidentes virtudes pero también defectos. Cold Simmetry ha sabido pulir y trasladar la experiencia original a una secuela infinitamente superior a su predecesor. Y es que Mortal Shell 2 es más largo, más variado, más divertido, más bonito y más complejo que su primera entrega. Y si tenemos en cuenta que el equipo de desarrollo principal es un grupo de solo 30 personas, el resultado es totalmente impresionante. Un mundo abierto bien construido, un diseño de niveles notable, multitud de mazmorras, rutas y secretos escondidos, armas, habilidades y shells variadas y satisfactorias, bosses correctos (no son malos pero tampoco destacan) y un combate y variedad de builds bastante profundo, hacen de este Mortal Shell 2 una experiencia muy satisfactoria. Con el género soulslike llenándose cada año de propuestas clónicas y que siguen los estándares al pie de la letra, valoro que Mortal Shell 2 se atreva a proponer sus propias mecánicas: el endurecimiento (esta vez más opcional que en el 1), el sistema de Shells (8 diferentes con su árbol de habilidades individual), la construcción de builds basada en objetos equipables y la subida de nivel uniforme (dejando atrás los atributos clásicos como fuerza o agilidad), su diseño y gore tan Heavy Metal, la introducción de armas de fuego, etc. El juego también tiene una duración perfecta: a ritmo normal, son unas 30 horas en ver los créditos. Para sacar el platino y hacer todo lo opcional, yo paré el reloj en 46h. La gestión de builds y progresión del personaje me ha recordado al infravalorado Remnant 2, otro buen soulslike con mucha personalidad. Y, por momentos, su diseño de niveles (como las mazmorras opcionales), su ambientación de fantasía oscura y la sensación de perderme en un mundo decadente, me ha transportado a Elden Ring y la trilogía Dark Souls. Como puntos negativos, diría que aún tiene algunos bugs molestos, que el NG+ no aporta mucho a día de hoy (supongo que lo arreglaran más adelante) y, como decía antes, que los bosses en general están bien pero podrían haber destacado más en sus mecánicas jugables. En resumen, para mi es un 8,5 pero le pongo un 9 porque se nota que los devs le han puesto corazón y trabajo al juego, porque se esfuerzan en tener su propia identidad dentro del género y porque han escuchado a la comunidad y han sacado parches rapidísimos para arreglar lo que no funcionaba de lanzamiento. Supongo que habrá una tercera parte, y si siguen mejorando la fórmula como han hecho con el 2, la saga tiene un muy buen futuro. Si te gustan los soulslikes, es fácil recomendarlo. No te decepcionará.

reviews.author: DBMcNeal
reviews.quote: First, I want to start off by having the utmost respect for Cold Symmetry and the team of just 30 developers that made Mortal Shell 2. This game is better than most AAA studios that have 9 figure budgets to work with, and I was genuinely impressed by the atmosphere and design choices of most of the game. Mortal Shell 2 has the most potential of any game that I ever played, and I think that if they did some things just a tad bit differently, it would’ve turned out to be a game of the year **** shell and tarstone systems are really cool systems, and I think this paired with the amazing exploration was the stand out of the game overall. Players can play this game however they want, for me, i went with a Tiel build with axe and dagger infused with blood curse (pretty generic) but I think Tiel was such a cool shell. About midway during my playthrough I used Proxima with the axekatana infused with lightning, and I had fun with that as well. However, I did run in to a lot of bugs/glitches, which I didn’t really care too much about, but I did have a problem with some of the boss designs as well as their movesets. I am a pretty avid “soulslike” gamer, so i didn’t have much trouble with any of the bosses (aside from the final boss). Two of the bosses stuck out to me as good design choices that I wish they would’ve stuck with more throughout the game.. Nameless Captive and Malborn Offspring. Outside of those two the Wandering Shepherd was pretty cool as well. When I think about how punchy and good the combat in this game feels, I look at Malborn Offspring and Nameless Captive to be the types of fights that works well with the combat system. On the other hand, I look at Hexapod, Magdelana, and Zmey as being the opposite. These 3 bosses were frustrating because they had such a limited moveset paired with the fact that they did not really force players to utilize the entirety of the good combat system the game has to offer. For example, against magdelana, you had pretty much nothing to parry so the fight itself was about avoiding her, hexapod was a fight of mostly dodging and if you didn’t dodge you would get one-shot, and Zmey was a combination of Magdelana and hexapod with a enormous health pool. Furthermore, the design choices of most of the mobs were decent but the movesets could’ve been a little more unpredictable, and I think getting one-shot by them to compensate for the lack of movesets was a very punishing decision the devs **** atmosphere and story of the game made things feel mysterious. I think they did such a good job of making you feel alone in such a ominous world. Also, Ruk was awesome, he’s easily the best character in Mortal Shell 2 and I wish we had more of him. The voice acting was top notch and he did a good job explaining to the harbinger what to expect from the journey ahead. Couple the atmosphere with the discovering of shells of lost warriors in cool dungeons with puzzles to get through and I was hooked. This level of exploration alone was enough for me to love this game and look past most of the flaws without really caring too much about it. (Circling back to my original statement of this being a game with the most potential that I ever played) I am looking forward to whatever sequel or dlc that is coming after all of the feedback provided from the community that loves this game. I think Cold Symmetry is sitting on gold with the “Mortal Shell” Title. I’m still blown away at how good it is with just a small team of developers. All in all this game was phenomenal and despite its flaws, I could recommend this to everyone who loves a challenge and loves open world games with deep exploration.

reviews.quote: This game exceeded my initial expectations. It’s a really great Souls-like, even if it’s simpler than others. reviews.author: SansEclat
reviews.quote:
Mortal Shell II has been one of my biggest surprises in recent years. I expected something much more limited and linear, almost like a cheaper version of Elden Ring, but instead I found a huge, interconnected world with a strong identity of its own. 

Exploration is genuinely rewarding, there are tons of areas and secrets to discover, and the different Shells, weapons and builds offer a lot of variety. The combat is extremely satisfying, and the game constantly makes me want to keep playing, explore one more area or unlock one more **** does have some flaws. 
The gameplay can occasionally feel inconsistent: movement can be a little unpredictable, you can sometimes fall or die in frustrating ways, and certain abilities — especially some clone AI — do not always work as reliably as they should. 
The draw distance and heavy use of fog can also be disappointing in some areas. 

Progression is another weakness: upgrading several Shells requires too much grinding, and the skill-point economy could definitely be better balanced.
The story itself is relatively simple, and the memories are not always presented in the most compelling way, but the atmosphere, world design and gameplay more than make up for it. The way the different regions connect is excellent, and I was genuinely surprised by how large and complete the game feels.

What I especially appreciate is the effort from Cold Symmetry. They clearly listen to player feedback, release fixes quickly, and still care about offering a complete physical release. You can feel the work and passion behind the game.

Despite its imperfections, none of them are serious enough to ruin the experience. Mortal Shell II has its own personality and is far more than an Elden Ring imitation. For me, it is easily one of the best games I have played in the last few years, and an extremely promising step forward for the studio.

reviews.author: Jagdwurst-Janik
reviews.quote:
Mortal Shell 2 is a massive step up from its predecessor. The combat feels satisfyingly heavy and impactful, the different Shells and weapons are a lot of fun to experiment with, and the open world genuinely rewards exploration.
Unfortunately, it still suffers from many of the same issues as the first game. The boss fights are incredibly frustrating and often feel more unfair than fun, enemy variety is severely lacking, and the map makes it far too easy to get completely lost instead of actually helping you figure out where to go.
Despite its flaws, Mortal Shell 2 is definitely a step in the right direction for Cold Symmetry. I’m excited to see what they do with their next game!

reviews.author: elDiego_0

Também encontrei muitos bugs, varios durante a exploração e alguns em boss fights. Durante a boss fight contra o Lost Child, meu personagem simplesmente teleportava para fora da arena do nada e contra o boss final, também tive problemas onde meu personagem perdia todas as armas e eu tive que resetar a luta varias vezes por isso. Splatoon Raiders of-fish-ally earns our seal of approval as a fantastic game in the franchise. Whether you go it alone or get help from other players, searching for loot and mining ore has never been so fun, thanks to the amount of weapons and gadgets you can equip to blast enemies out of existence. Plus, you get to hang out with Deep Cut, which is always a fun time.

Splatoon Raiders is a wonderful solo reinvention of the popular multiplayer series filled with smartly designed missions and endlessly engaging progression systems. Underpinned by the franchise’s fantastic shooting mechanics, it’s a fresh and exciting adventure that should be in every Nintendo Switch 2 owner’s library.

Splatoon Raiders doesn't take itself too seriously and knows its audience. It's not trying to redefine gaming, it's just a fun, lighthearted ride that doesn't underestimate the audience or hold back on its mechanics.

You know you’ve hit gold when your biggest criticism of a game is that you just wanted more. Between the fast-paced, technical gameplay, the depth of the build mechanics, and the irreverent design that underpins the Splatoon series, this is an experience that’s shockingly hard to fault. Go play it.

Splatoon Raiders successfully twists the Splatoon formula into a slick, satisfying single player-focused looter shooter that's incredibly difficult to put down. Surprisingly deep loot game, some absolutely hectic encounters and a bleakly-beachy vibe all its own, there's plenty here for fans as well as anyone previously put off by the series' multiplayer focus.

Splatoon Raiders marks an excellent entry to the Splatoon franchise I’d wager, and anybody that enjoyed the previous  games but might’ve wanted a more fleshed out solo experience is gonna have a blast here. It might be a little repetitive if you’re not familiar with this style of looter gameplay, but otherwise it’s a fantastic experience. From the blend of stick aiming and gyro aiming to the fun soundtrack these games always offer and all the way down to the core gameplay, Raiders is an addictive title well worth playing. Personally, I’d wager I like it just a little more than the standard Splatoon titles if not solely for the fact I’m definitely not as good at Splatoon than other kinds of shooters. Existing Splatoon fans will have a great time with Splatoon Raiders, but for new fans or anybody interested in Splatoon it’s probably the best way to get into the series in a solo environment before you decide to make the plunge into the main games.

Smart progression, perfect balance, a charismatic story and characters, lots of post-game content and mechanics that will make you sink hours into without even noticing the time go by. Splatoon Riders is here to stay, proving that its campaign mode, whether played solo, in local co-op, or online, is just as fun as the previous PVP focused titles.

Splatoon Raiders offers excellent value for money, with plenty of variety to cater to different types of players. The main campaign delivers a more curated adventure with a steady learning curve that’s made even more enjoyable by teaming up with friends or strangers online. Once the credits roll, the post-game content shifts gears, giving hardcore players an endless chase for increasingly difficult scenarios and better loot that’s genuinely hard to put down. Splatoon Raiders, in my opinion, was a very risky move for a franchise that’s still growing its playerbase, but Nintendo has managed to defy expectations by delivering a solo Splatoon adventure with plenty of bait on the hook. Rather than simply serving as another Side Order, Splatoon Raiders inks its own identity in spectacular fashion, and it’s safe to say this adventure has me hook, line and sinker.

Splatoon Raiders is a gamble that paid off. Nintendo takes one of its most recognizable franchises and has the courage to steer it in a completely different direction without betraying its identity. Ink, movement, and chaotic combat remain at the heart of the experience, yet a surprisingly deep progression system emerges around these elements—one capable of winning over even those who usually view looter-shooters with skepticism. A bit too much grinding, a structure prone to repetition, and a narrative that falls short of the game world's full potential keep the title from achieving perfection. Yet, Raiders proves something important: Splatoon is not merely a brilliant competitive arena, but a world still brimming with possibilities. And this spin-off is concrete proof that Nintendo was right to explore them.

The characters themselves are also a huge highlight. The gameplay is just as addictive as you'd expect from a looter-shooter. Splatoon Raiders takes the consistently improved upon gameplay of the Salmon Run side game and perfects it by introducing a continuously engaging story mode, countless items to collect and upgrade, and multiple gameplay styles to beat each challenge the game throws at you to give equal entertainment no matter the type of player you are. The core gameplay loop is incredible, as you explore more of the map taking on different types of missions, you're constantly getting more powerful in unique ways, from simple things like more weapon damage to equipping upgrades which provide your gadgets with interesting gimmicks like exploding when throwing them on the battlefield or being able to use them twice at a time. 

The music does a good job setting the tone, with what many have come to expect in the post-apocalyptic and rigid world of Splatoon, but with its own flair, and is some of the best the series has to offer.

If you are a fan of looter shooters, or maybe tired of their repetitive gameplay and are looking for something bolder or new, Splatoon Raiders is an excellent new take on the genre which I can't recommend enough.
