Fields of Mistria is everything I look for in a farming sim, combining a lively village, strong characters, satisfying progression, and an addictive gameplay loop. The 1.0 release builds beautifully on the already impressive early access version, with improved day length, better quality-of-life features, and more room for the story to grow. Minor issues like some post-update lag and a slightly underwhelming museum barely hold it back. For me, Fields of Mistria is one of the best farming sims right now, with gorgeous pixel art, memorable NPCs, and a world I’m far from done exploring.

Fields of Mistria is an exceptional farming game sim that stands tall among titles like Stardew Valley and the best Story of Seasons entries. It’s gorgeous. The gameplay loop is sharp. The characters are lovable. The sense of growth and progression is satisfying. Fields of Mistria is a fantastic way to spend 20, 50, or 100 hours of your life.

Fields of Mistria is a rare farming RPG that manages to improve upon the genre's familiar foundations without losing what made them so appealing in the first place. Its farming, RPG progression, relationships, exploration, and narrative all complement one another, creating an experience where nearly every activity contributes to the larger journey. A few rough edges in combat, resource RNG, and quality-of-life keep it from absolute perfection, but they do little to diminish an otherwise remarkably polished and thoughtfully designed experience. Fields of Mistria doesn't just prove that the genre still has room to grow, it sets an incredibly high bar for what a modern farming RPG can be.
A fresh face for farm sims that brings the magic back with the best-written cast I've seen from the genre.
NPC Studio delivers a community-bonding experience and the chance to live out your Sailor Senshi dreams, all from the comfort of the farmstead.

I would never wish to slander the good name of Stardew Valley, for it breathed new life into a genre that was unfairly left to decay. Nonetheless, let it be said that Fields of Misteria is now the new standard by which I’ll measure every other experience within the genre. It’s not going to be easy to beat the attention to detail so meticulously thought through here. To those looking to rival this newcomer, I suggest you do your research to make damn sure you have something equally as enjoyable to challenge Fields of Mistria with.  [Early Access Score = 90]
Simply put, Fields of Mistria is magic — and it’s not even done yet.

Fields of Mistria is incredibly polished for an Early Access game. It boasts a charming cast of fleshed out, loveable characters, and an impressive amount of customisation for both player characters and decoration. The gameplay balances a nice balance between quality of life features, new twists to a well-known formula, and nostalgia. If you are looking for a stand-out title in the farming-sim genre, Fields of Mistria is sure to delight. [Early Access Score = 90]

Fields of Mistria doesn't hide its inspirations and brings together favorite elements of farming simulator enthusiasts, combined with conveniences that were previously only possible with community modifications. It's a gem yet to be polished, but it already shows high quality in its development version. [Early Access Review Score = 90]]

I went into Fields of Mistria expecting something fairly routine. I’ve played a lot of games like this before, and nothing I’d seen of it in the lead-up led me to think Mistria would be anything special. It’s weird to be both right and wrong about this. Fields of Mistria really is a lot of what I’m already very familiar with, polished up and sparkling. But it’s also got a charge to it, a brightness that’s compelling me to stay even when I feel I already know every trick it could possibly pull. Another spring, summer, fall, and winter in Mistria are waiting for me, and though I already know what bounties they’ll bring, I’m willing to be surprised by them anyway.

To Nintendo fans who haven’t experienced Kingdom Hearts in its full splendor, this is an incredible time to jump in. These games are largely excellent action RPGs that are jam-packed with an out-there emotional story filled with oodles of Disney and Square Enix references.

This new collection cements the Nintendo Switch 2’s reputation as a great console for third-party ports, with a impressive array of games that look and run spectacularly even in handheld mode, particularly the most visually stunning of them all, Kingdom Hearts III.

Overall, Kingdom Hearts Collection 1-3 on Switch 2 is a fantastic package that is so close to being completely on par with the Integrum Masterpiece release. Kingdom Hearts 3 and A Fragmentary Passage’s framerate issues are the only things stopping it from definitively being my new favourite way to play, but the ability to go portable is worth those minor issues. Whether you’re a complete newcomer preparing for Kingdom Hearts 4 or a diehard fan like me looking for an excuse to replay, Kingdom Hearts Collection 1-3 on Switch 2 is a fantastic way to do it.

KINGDOM HEARTS Collection [I~III] is an ambitious, emotionally resonant package that highlights the series’ remarkable highs, messy experiments, and constant reinvention. Its native Switch 2 release finally fixes one of the franchise’s biggest accessibility problems, while Critical Mode, Re Mind, and years of updates make Kingdom Hearts III far stronger than it was at launch. However, uneven world design, inconsistent combat systems across entries, performance hiccups on Switch 2, and the continued absence of playable 358/2 Days, Re:coded, Melody of Memory, and the full χ saga prevent this from feeling truly definitive.

Kingdom Hearts Collection [I~III] is an excellent way to experience most of the Kingdom Hearts franchise, whether for the first time or for the umpteenth. Most of the bundled games deliver essentially perfect performance on the Nintendo Switch 2, while the more recent games still maintain consistent enough frame rates to please most. Being able to play the entire franchise on the go is a thrilling prospect, and I’ll likely be doing so for a good long while to come. This is a great way to get ready for Kingdom Hearts IV, and I’m sure many Nintendo-exclusive fans will be doing just that with this top-notch bundle.

Kingdom Hearts Collection [I～III] is an incredible package that brings nearly the entire saga together in one place. I would have liked to see a performance and frame rate toggle for Kingdom Hearts III, and the $75 asking price is a little steep considering how cheap this collection is on other platforms. At the end of the day, though, it’s Kingdom Hearts finally on Switch 2, and it’s hard to ask for much more.
KINGDOM HEARTS Collection (I-III) gives owners of the Nintendo Switch 2 a fantastic collection of games that all run superbly on the hardware. It is finally here!

Kingdom Hearts Collection [I–III] is the definitive collection of the series, offering everything fans need to know to prepare for the fourth numbered entry. A highlight is the Switch 2 version, which finally allows console owners to run the games natively and with good performance.

The Kingdom Hearts Collection [1~3] is the definitive way to experience the saga, offering polished ports and nearly the entire lore on Nintendo Switch 2. Despite minor performance dips, it’s the best entry point for newcomers and a nostalgic return for veterans.
KINGDOM HEARTS Collection [I~III] is a wonderful bundle of everything Kingdom Hearts, and on the Switch 2 it's just perfection.

The Coalition has elevated the franchise to new heights, crafting an engaging, brutal, and surprisingly intimate campaign that’s full of smart gameplay mechanics and wonderful surprises. It’s the best Gears has ever felt to play, and the best it’s ever looked and sounded on the big screen. Gears of War: E-Day? It's a f.cking masterpiece.

Gears of War: E-Day is, for me, the best game in the series and The Coalition's finest work to date. Its campaign brings Marcus and Dom back without relying solely on nostalgia, delivering a darker and more brutal take on the origins of the Locust threat.

Gears of War: E-Day is a monumental triumph from a developer that irrefutably understands what’s important to fans: Gears isn’t just about tearing through Locust with a chainsaw, it’s about brotherhood, sacrifice, and grief. The Coalition has delivered an unforgettable campaign packed full of fresh ideas whilst staying true to what makes Gears so special. The Locust are back and more terrifying than ever, and blasting them to bits is incredibly satisfying. This is the best the combat has felt in twenty years, and fighting to survive the fall of Kalona will leave you speechless. Through its stunning locations, characters, and cinematics, E-Day is a visual powerhouse and one of the best-looking games I’ve ever seen on Xbox.

Weapons of all kinds, gadgets, and locations brimming with possibilities form the foundation of a story that excels in every aspect. Marcus and Dom return alongside old and new acquaintances in a prequel that feels fresh and invigorating. The story of Kalona’s downfall on E-Day serves as the starting point for a war-torn odyssey filled with unique situations, memorable scenes, and the feeling of experiencing an iconic moment in a saga that, for many, is a must-play. Gears of War: E-Day marks a turning point for the Xbox catalog with a console and PC exclusive that’s determined to raise the bar for Microsoft.
A campaign executed to perfection in terms of both technical aspects and gameplay. A brutal and intense war spectacle featuring the best Gears story to date.

I have to say that Gears of War: E-Day is an absolute triumph of a game. The maps in the multiplayer and the campaign are big, with things to find in unlikely corners. From there, exploration in the story mode should be seen as its own reward. This is a game full of content, and you’ll spend hours upon hours taking in everything it has to offer.  Whether you’re here for the campaign, or prefer to get invested in the multiplayer, if you have the slightest interest in Gears, you have to play Gears of War: E-Day. It really is that simple.

Gears of War: E-Day delivers arguably the franchise's finest, most atmospheric campaign, brilliantly balancing pulse-pounding action with genuine horror roots. By pairing breathtaking Series X visuals and refined combat with a deeply emotional return to Marcus and Dom, The Coalition has delivered a masterclass prequel that restores complete faith in Xbox's future. A triumph from start to finish.

Gears of War: E-Day shines by showing off humanity's perseverance. Every new character stands out, never overshadowed by the legacy of Marcus or Dom. Even with the game taking place in one city over several days, the evolution of that city and its inhabitants has created fleshed-out characters that you're rooting for the success of every step of the way.

E-Day succeeds in telling the story of Emergence Day in a gripping, desperate, and most importantly, fun way. The culmination of 20 years as a franchise, refining everything the series is into a must-play XBOX title that takes you on a gloriously brutal, emotionally-satisfying, and epic, cinematic adventure.

Gears of War: E-Day delivers arguably the series’ strongest campaign, combining mature, restrained storytelling with the return of Marcus Fenix’s charismatic presence. Already among the franchise’s finest entries, it could become a serious Game of the Year contender if its content-rich multiplayer matches the campaign’s quality. Regardless, Xbox players should not miss this outstanding return to form.

reviews.author: ktatosfatih
reviews.quote: The first two hours of the game, which I'd consider its opening act, are absolutely phenomenal. It starts off with an atmosphere and level of seriousness that far exceeded my **** the game progressed, almost every time I found myself wondering, "Is this going to get repetitive?", I was introduced to new weapons, new weapon attachments, a wide variety of enemies, and occasional light semi-open-world elements that were implemented with just the right balance. This variety largely eliminated my concerns about the game becoming repetitive.I also really enjoyed the sequences in certain parts of some chapters where the game intentionally slows down the pace to put more emphasis on character interactions and dialogue. These quieter sections, which allow you to appreciate the game's atmosphere, stunning visuals, and explore the environments, provide a great balance to the overall experience.Towards the finale, the intensity ramps up significantly. That said, there are a few combat sequences where the game starts to feel somewhat repetitive and monotonous. However, looking at the experience as a whole, I think the overall pacing is handled exceptionally well.I played the entire game from start to finish in co-op, and it reminded me just how much I've missed experiencing story-driven games with a friend. Playing through this game with someone else definitely makes the experience even more enjoyable.Overall, it's an incredibly fun, pure action game. And I really want to emphasize that point: **This is a pure action game.** Rather than expecting deep RPG mechanics or hundreds of hours of open-world content, if you're looking for satisfying gunplay, fast-paced gameplay, plenty of intense firefights, and big-budget cinematic action, that's exactly what this game delivers.I genuinely believe that anyone who enjoys pure action games should give this one a chance. If you're looking for a high-budget shooter packed with epic moments and focused on delivering action from beginning to end, I can wholeheartedly recommend it.

reviews.author: LancerPelican
reviews.quote:
What I liked: The city of Kalona and watching it fall and become utterly destroyed over the coarse of the campaign. Level design was nice. The gameplay was fun. The progression was good with weapon mods and upgrades. The overall plot of E-Day was great. Daan Riggs, the Kemara Twins and Tai Kaliso stood out the most as side characters. Horde Siege is very fun but could be further expanded upon in scale and depth. 

Why this game falls flat: Marcus and Dom do NOT feel like the leads at all. Especially if you 100% the campaign and experience everything the campaign and to offer the dialogues that are spoken within the main squad. The relationship between them doesn’t really change or grow until the very last chapter. Dom especially was written like a stale tomato and nothing like how he was in the first three games. Provides minimal commentary, some input here and there… that’s it. I’ve no clue how anyone could’ve approved writing a legacy franchise character like this and pushed this background role on him. Marcus too largely takes a backseat up until the very end as well. So who are the actual main focusses of the story? The Coalition new original character Mags Carter. What’s frustrating is not only the fact that she had a larger focus as you progress through the campaign but there’s absolutely nothing redeeming about her. She is so boring, uninteresting, and written like they are born of pessimism. Lucas isn’t great either. And just like Gears 4 and 5, the studio fails to write actual meaningful dialogue. In one section in the main campaign after defeating the frog like enemies, Lucas literally yells “well that was… something”. Are you fr? Another section in the final chapters after flipping a switch to cross a crane in the docks. AS THE PLATFORM IS TURNING IN FRONT OF YOU Mags has to let the player know “the platform is turning we should be able to cross” like no kidding thanks? Or during Act 3 while riding a sky train, after crashing and getting off she will say “always hated riding the train”. What is this man? But fine… fine if you want to ignore something like that because it’s a little nitpicky and incessant alright. But what you can’t ignore is their utterly dull personalities. Mags is constantly pessimistic. Always complaining and dumping her past experiences in the cog every chance she gets. When the cog soldiers on the bridge make fun of Lucas for being a by the book soldier she shoots it down and tells him to not listen to them everyone goes through it. Can we not make a joke? But in the same act proceeds to make fun him herself on many occasions lmao. This writing doesn’t add anything to the characters at all. I thought Lucas would be a character who gives us an outlook of E-Day through someone who’s never seen the horrors of the pendulum wars and war in general. At first it seemed to be going that way in Act 1 but went NO WHERE after that. He was desensitized to it all immediately and just asked basic questions here and there. A scene in act 4 also took a lot of seriousness out. We come to learn Lucas broke strict protocol and mentions how he wanted to experience being on the front lines of the Pendulum wars with his friends, so he decided to hold a prolonged communication with his old friends as they were fighting the UIR. Turns out the indies tracked the signal and they all died because of him. At first, you see how that experience really broke him. Understandable. But what utterly destroyed this scene was Mags coming in saying how “we all get it wrong.” SERIOUSLY LOL? Get it wrong lol? Writing like this just never felt like the game could be taken seriously. In act 3 Marcus tells Mags who he’s barely known for 2 days about the truth behind Carlos LMAO. 

The final fight was very average feeling like a modernized version of RAAMs fight in Gears 1, and the story overall felt rushed towards the end and didn’t really land. The open sections and acts 2-4 were also very bare bones. They were very detailed and looked stunning, but had no substance in them. The over abundance of hard cases all over these maps was very frustrating to grab and I don’t understand how anyone can find all of them without looking at a guide.

Overall, I feel like this game is best to play using gamepass or grab on sale. I cannot believe they charged $100 for a FOMO edition. Let alone the base $70 price tag. I do believe this game can be a solid foundation for what comes next as they’ve already built out a lot of what they would need for future installments. That is if the studio gets another shot after this. The Gears franchise has been in a niche corner for a LONG time. And with the creative decisions they’re making some good but still a lot more bad I don’t know who this franchise is for anymore. Newer audiences have no interest in Gears of War. And we can see that with data on the last three games. And the core audience seems to be fading as well. At this point just remake Gears 2 and let the franchise rest

reviews.author: Essiach
reviews.quote: Absolute disgrace to the franchise! This is not the OG Gears we all remember...

For me, Star Wars: Galactic Racer has become the perfect arcade racing game experience that leaves nothing to be desired. The sense of speed is the best it’s been since the first WipeOut, and it not only looks stunning, but sounds and plays that way, too. Even if you’re not a huge Star Wars fan, you should check out this game if only for its fresh roguelite ideas and the gripping campaign mode, which completely reinvents and revitalizes the sci-fi racing genre in turbo-boost mode.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer is not only one of the best racing games I have played all year, but after playing the campaign the full way through, it just might be one of my favourite racing games of all time.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer absolutely nails what it is trying to do. It is a high-octane racer that's endless fun to play, and it looks fantastic. This would have been a great game with a standard single-player mode, but what is here is inventive and engaging. I'd have loved a few silly classic characters and another planet or two, but this is a game I'll return to for a long time.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer is everything I hoped it would be. Fuse built a campaign that keeps giving me reasons to master the tracks, then made the racing feel good enough that I wanted to.  And for my fellow Episode I Racer lovers: Galactic Racer’s marketing has kept the podracers in the background, but don’t let that fool you. By the time I was done with the campaign, I found myself happy and whispering one thing to myself: Now this is podracing.

These worlds don't just look beautiful, from Jakku's dunes and wrecked Star Destroyers you must thread between to Crait's white crystalline surface with red dust billowing underneath. They're also carved up into fascinating tracks that blend tight underground corridors where cornering is a constant discussion with death, and daringly wide-open outside sections where I once got so turned around I ended up going backwards. These are places that constantly shift in the way that they challenge you, and I suspect that better racers than me will spend an awfully long time working out the optimal strategies for handling each one.

Star Wars Galactic Racer is a Star-Wars-authentic thrill rush that may be the best racer in a decade. It’s such a wonderful, engaging experience that literally does everything right. Just be warned – as a roguelite – the on-ramp can take time while presenting a higher difficulty level.

While the lack of local multiplayer is unfortunate, the decision to drop the mode so that the game is kept at a locked frame-rate is the right one. The game is so fast-paced that you need every millisecond possible. The tracks are all excellent, the music and sound effects are jaw-dropping, and both gameplay and customization have a ton of depth. The single player campaign is surprisingly good and has a lot more under the hood than I was expecting. Its roguelike elements are well-thought out, and will keep you coming back for more well after you beat the game. Online multiplayer has a variety of modes, from traditional arcade style races to entire tours across the galaxy, so that every type of player can find something to enjoy. Overall, Star Wars: Galactic Racer has just the right amount of nostalgia, and is a true evolution of the podracing experience. It’s frenetic, bombastic, and above all else, incredibly fun.

Star Wars Galactic Racer is a spectacular surprise and a must-play for racing and Star Wars fans. It shines with exhilarating speed, excellent online support, a smart build system, and a fantastic dose of Podracing nostalgia. While its roguelite structure may not appeal to those looking for a traditional campaign, the quality of its racing and combat makes it one of the best Star Wars games in recent years.

Fuse Games have truly given Millennial gamers like myself that spiritual successor to Star Wars Episode I: Racer that we never got. And to them, I give them all the grace that a post-Empire galaxy allows us.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer is a spectacular and surprisingly thrilling racing game that delivers an excellent Star Wars experience through its run-based gameplay, strategic choices, and spectacular crashes.

reviews.author: MagMachina
reviews.quote: Oh how i wish i would love this game more. First the most important thing, SPEED and FEEL: People say it's fast, but i have to disagree. This game, on the other hand, only gives you the impression of speed, while the tracks themselves feel small. Then there’s the handling: the racers feel floaty, sloppy and soft to control. I miss the highly precise, sharp-edged handling of the really good old-school sci-fi racing games. Then there are the absurd DESIGN DECISIONS: no split-screen multiplayer, no option to select individual tracks, no time trials, no maps, and the decision to turn the Pod Racers into a separate game within the game. And finally, the TRACKS themselves: there simply aren’t enough of them, and they aren’t particularly creative. Another comparison to Episode I: Racer — there were sandcrawlers on the track, Tusken Raiders shooting at you, traps, and anti-gravity tunnels. Why do the tracks in a Star Wars racing game have to be so boring and unimaginative? Another criticism is the CAMPAIGN. It’s certainly creative, but I don’t need constant story interruptions in an arcade racer. I want to race, not chat with mechanics and other characters. I thought a Star Wars Racer from a Burnout-Team would be my dream game (i loved the Burnout-games!). Now i hope for some patches and updates, because i wont play this game much longer...

True, beating the main storyline of Bubbly Basin didn't take me too long. I finished it in a couple of evenings, but I am far from done with all the extras. There is so much to do, and so many Pokémon to find. Honestly, just the fact that even as I write this review, all I want to do is go back and play Pokémon Pokopia: Bubbly Basin should be enough to show how much I enjoy it.

Pokémon Pokopia just keeps getting better with the release of Bubbly Basin – the first of three DLC areas that has set an exceptional standard for those yet to be released. There’s lots to explore and more charming narrative content, as well as a strong selection of Pokémon to befriend. If you enjoyed Pokémon Pokopia’s base game, you’d be missing out by passing on Bubbly Basin, and I can’t wait to see what the next area is like.

Part one of the Pokémon Pokopia DLC, Bubbly Basin, is an exciting addition to an already fabulous game. You’ll meet new Pokémon, explore a new area, and spend even more hours rebuilding and having fun.
Bubbly Basin is a delightful new underwater area to dive into in Pokémon Pokopia, which promises hours of salty fun with your favourite water types.

okémon Pokopia Expansion Pass Part 1 – Bubbly Basin is an easy recommendation for those who love the base game. It adds an exciting new area, new movement, and plenty more Pokémon to hang out with. While the question of the rest of the expansion pass’s parts lingers, Bubbly Basin is a fantastic start to it, adding tons of hours to an already incredible experience.
An excellent slice of DLC that, just like the parent game, manages to comfortably exceed expectations, with a large new map and an impressive array of new pokémon, objects, and features.

Bubbly Basin is a rather pleasant surprise. Sure, it follows the established formula and doesn’t stray too far from it, but it’s clear that a lot of care has gone into making this underwater adventure feel like a natural extension of Pokopia. From the calming exploration and gorgeous environments to the new Pokémon, crafting opportunities and the remnants of Curellian City, there’s plenty here to keep you coming back for more.

In the end, the Bubbly Basin DLC is a straightforward extension of the same gameplay loop that defined Pokopia. But that’s one of its great strengths. For the hardcore players who can’t put this game down, a whole new biome is a precious gift. The dive mechanic and the upgraded storage are lovely perks, but a huge new map to play around in? A new space to fill up with cute houses, crumbling ruins, and impossible temples? It’s everything I hoped for. This DLC won’t convert anyone to the cause. And if you were overwhelmed by your options, having a new biome certainly won’t help. But for the dedicated players, Bubbly Basin is a vital infusion of new content. If you’re already invested in the base game, you simply can’t let this expansion pass you by.
Bubbly Basin highlights the strengths of underwater Pokémon spectacularly with its new area, but its story missions lack detail.

Pokémon Pokopia: Bubble Blub Depths confirms that Omega Force’s title is one of the year's best games. This DLC improves upon all the mechanics seen in Pokémon Pokopia and prompts reflection on a future that is as imminent as it is inevitable if we continue to treat our planet the way we do. The decision to set the entire game underwater allows it to unfold across multiple levels and make the most of the most widespread Pokémon fauna: Water types.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve exemplifies “High-Flying Action” and takes it to another level, while also giving new fans options to ease into it. Personally, I say dive into the deep end; flying directly into the ground a few times puts some hair on your chest. If you enjoy exploring an action game in a massive 3D space, love jets and airplanes, or are already a fan of the franchise, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a masterclass in its category.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a bold evolution of the foundation laid in AC7. Its story is more exciting, its presentation is more polished, and most importantly, its gameplay is impeccable, with a variety of missions and combat situations that keep the player engaged, entertained, and wanting more. This is one of the best games not only of the year, but of the generation.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve elevates the franchise to new heights with a spectacular campaign that mixes high octane missions with relevant thematic storytelling. The real ace, though, remains the compelling and addictive dogfighting gameplay.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is an improvement in everything that is quintessentially “Ace Combat," bringing back squadron commands and adding a plethora of different aircraft, new special weapons, and more. The cinematic visuals and deep, twisting narrative immerse the player in the fantasy of being an ace pilot in a war between two nations.
Ace Combat 8 is a love letter to combat aviation in its entirety. It showcases aircraft as bringers of both death and salvation, but from an earnest, human perspective.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a spectacular return for the long-running flight combat series, combining exceptionally responsive controls with stunning audiovisual presentation and a substantial 30-mission campaign. Its blend of accessible arcade action and deeper simulation elements makes every dogfight satisfying, while an engaging story, extensive aircraft customization, and multiplayer provide plenty of longevity. Upgrades can feel unnecessary on standard difficulty, but this is otherwise an impressively complete package and one of the strongest flight combat games of the modern era.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve gives you total freedom in how you fly and fight, with plenty of customisation options and visuals that'll blow you away.

The years roll by—now counted in decades given the series' longevity—yet it is delightful to see Ace Combat endure as a franchise crafted with passion and love for both video games and its loyal fanbase. Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve stands as one of the franchise's finest entries, undoubtedly earning a spot in the conversation for the series' greatest title of all time. From the very start, it is a beautiful, fun, and challenging game that captures the true essence of gaming through its focus on design and mechanics. Project Aces—now Bandai Namco Aces—remains true to its vision without compromising its identity. Without a doubt, this is one of the year's best games and an experience not to be missed.

After 30 years of soaring to new heights, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve finally reaches the summit and stands undisputed. Refined in every possible way, it is not only the finest game in the series to date, but arguably one of the greatest air combat simulations ever made.

ACE Combat 8: Wings of the Theve from Bandai Namco Aces Inc. is a marvelous, beautiful dogfighting flight simulator. It offers a solid storyline with real stakes, a good variety of missions to keep the game engaging and fun, and accessible gameplay that should satisfy both newbies and veterans of the series.

reviews.author: Arima_
OmniGodEmperor
reviews.quote:
METACRITIC REVIEW | 10/10

I have been in the skies of Strangereal since Air Combat on the original PlayStation. I have completed every entry in the franchise. After 145 hours with Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, including achieving Platinum with the ultra rare Ace of Aces trophy requiring S rank on every mission at ACE difficulty, I can say without hesitation that Wings of Theve is the best Ace Combat game ever made. It surpasses Ace Combat 5: The Unsung War, which held that title for over two decades in my personal ranking.

Storyline

Project Aces has consistently delivered narratives that punch above the weight of what an aerial combat game should be capable of producing. Wings of Theve continues that tradition at the highest level the series has ever reached. The story respects franchise lore, advances the Strangereal timeline in a direction that has longtime fans watching the approach toward Ace Combat 3 Electrosphere territory with genuine excitement, and delivers emotional beats that land because the character work earns them. For players new to the series, it functions as a compelling standalone entry. For veterans who have followed Strangereal for decades, it rewards that investment meaningfully.

Gameplay

The moment to moment aerial combat is the most refined the series has delivered. The new control scheme is accessible for new players entering the franchise and represents a genuine design consideration for that audience. Veteran players who prefer the classic framework have Type B available and I returned to it immediately. Both work. The choice existing is the right decision.
The ACE difficulty S rank requirement is exactly what the series needed. This is not a participation trophy challenge. Clearing every mission including free missions at ACE with S rank demands genuine mechanical mastery of the aircraft, weapon systems, and mission design. The Ace of Aces trophy sitting at 0.3% rarity at time of writing reflects exactly how demanding that requirement is. It is the kind of challenge that justifies extended time investment and delivers genuine satisfaction when completed.

Music

Everflow and Hortus Regis Alti belong in the conversation for best tracks in the franchise's history, and Ace Combat's musical history is exceptional. The soundtrack as a whole is phenomenal and serves both the combat sequences and the narrative moments with the tonal precision the series has always delivered.

Technical Performance

Reviewed on base PS5, LG OLED G3 in Game Optimizer HGiG mode, and Samsung HW-Q990D in Game Mode Pro. The game performs beautifully on base hardware. The PS5 Pro Enhanced version likely elevates this further but the base experience is polished and visually strong throughout.

Content and Longevity

145 hours in and the Campaign Medal completions and online content still remain. The MRP grind for the 25,000,000 total required for trophy purposes alone represents substantial content engagement. The upcoming super aircraft DLCs are something I am genuinely looking forward to, as the franchise tradition of legendary aircraft additions has always extended the experience meaningfully.

For New and Returning Players

Wings of Theve works as both a franchise entry point and a veteran celebration. New players get a complete, compelling aerial combat experience with an accessible control option. Returning players get a love letter to everything that has made Strangereal one of gaming's most underappreciated fictional universes.

The AC3 Question

The timeline is approaching Electrosphere territory. Project Aces, if you are reading reviews: do not remaster. Remake. Ace Combat 3 deserves the full treatment and Wings of Theve has proven the team is capable of delivering it at the highest level.

10/10. The best Ace Combat game ever made. Essential for fans of the series and a genuine recommendation for anyone who has never played one. Get in the cockpit.

One of the Best Ace Combat Experiences I've Ever Had

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is one of the best Ace Combat games I've ever played. What makes it so special is the way it combines excellent mission design, memorable characters, and an incredible musical experience to create some genuinely unforgettable moments.

The mission design is fantastic, but what really elevates the experience is how the gameplay, story, and music come together during combat. The music that kicks in when facing certain enemies is especially effective. There are moments when everything clicks perfectly, the intensity rises, and you get genuine chills while your adrenaline goes through the roof. These aren't just cool action sequences; they're moments that make you feel completely immersed in the battle. The character designs are also excellent, adding another layer of personality to an already memorable experience. It's impressive how much emotional impact the game can deliver while you're right in the middle of an aerial dogfight.

For me, this is what Ace Combat is all about: thrilling air combat combined with cinematic storytelling and a soundtrack that knows exactly when to hit you with maximum impact. When all these elements come together, the result is something truly special.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is easily one of my favorite entries in the series. It reminded me why I love this franchise in the first place, and I won't soon forget some of the moments it gave me. A fantastic experience for any Ace Combat fan.

People have called Welcome to Elderfield the spiritual successor to Graveyard Keeper, but I think it deserves the accolade of being called the spiritual dark successor to Stardew Valley. Stardew Valley is considered the gold standard for narrative-driven farming sims, and in my opinion, Welcome to Elderfield has shown that it has what it takes to stand alongside the greats.

Welcome to Elderfield surprised me as a delightfully spooky, terror-filled take on the cozy farming sim genre. Depicting small-town life as full of unexplainable phenomena and horrors that become the mundane, Welcome to Elderfield easily shines as one of the most unique titles in its genre, while still delivering the familiar mechanics and gameplay loops that fans have come to expect.

Welcome to Elderfield draws you in with its slimy tentacles and grim aesthetic, but it is the challenging gameplay that truly keeps you hooked. Chris Cote masterfully combines humor, horror and tranquility, creating an experience that feels both relaxing and deeply unsettling. Elderfield may be impossible to leave, but after playing it, I wouldn't want to anyway.

The secrets of the town, its residents, its mysteries, and its atmosphere are meticulously crafted. Welcome to Elderfield succeeds at making horror and cozy farming-sim comfort coexist without either one undercutting the other. Its art direction is distinctive, its atmosphere is relentless in the best way, and its willingness to treat the abnormal as mundane gives it a personality unlike anything else currently in the genre. Some rough progression clarity and a few lingering bugs are the price of its ambition, but they’re minor blemishes on what is otherwise one of the most confident and original debuts of the year. If you’ve ever wanted your farming sim to also make your skin crawl, Welcome to Elderfield delivers that in spades.

It is very hard to stand out in video games as a whole, let alone in the farming sim genre. Welcome to Elderfield takes the main gameplay loop of the genre, dips it in grimdark horror, adds a dash of excellent sound and aesthetics, and the result is something that feels truly impressive.

Welcome to Elderfield from developer Chris Cote and publisher Kwalee is a horror-filled cozy game that offers plenty of questing content, a well-designed farming and crafting system, and features just enough turn-based combat to deliver a cornucopia of fun. While it has a few minor, correctable issues, it’s an enjoyable overall gameplay experience.

Welcome to Elderfield is a game worthy of the Lovecraftian title. It makes the mythos feel like a dark fairytale that you can take part in, and the weirdness of the whole experience is brilliant. Every little task feels rewarding because you get information, items, or access to resources. I put hours into this game, and I still don't know how I'm supposed to feel about it. If you're like me and enjoy both horror games and cozy games, then you definitely need to give it a try.

Welcome to Elderfield is impressive due to how many layers it contains. From the weeks I have spent with the game, I am still nowhere near uncovering all its secrets. The way that it juxtaposes wholesome activities, such as fishing and farming, with creepy elements and humour shows how much time solo developer Chris Cote has put into making Elderfield feel as alive as possible. Though some elements of the game need to be better explained, and some extra support may be needed due to the size of the playable spaces, the positives, such as how expansive the town and its secrets are, the dialogue and the creepy/cute aesthetics, make up for the confusion I experienced. Though I have written this review, I know my time with Welcome to Elderfield isn’t over yet. There is still a lot of world for me to be creeped out by…

Welcome to Elderfield is a game that proudly celebrates the things that inspired it. From its sense of exploration to its visual design and subtle storytelling, it’s clear that it was created by people who genuinely love this kind of thing. If you’re a fan of the mysterious and supernatural, this town will feel like your second home.
The words horror and cosy really shouldn’t go together and they absolutely shouldn’t work, but in Welcome to Elderfield they somehow find a horrifyingly happy medium.

Tukoni: Forest Keepers might be the best modern point-and-click title for someone who’s looking to see what the genre has to offer without being overwhelmed. The world is filled with curious and fun characters, the game looks beautiful, and the puzzle design is good without focusing on complexity. The Traveller isn’t a big personality, but he’s a happy problem solver who loves tea, so it’s easy to like him. Many players will be disappointed at how short the experience is. But it’s packed with good ideas and wholesome interactions. Play Tukoni: Forest Keepers in short sessions, savor the exploration, and maybe get into making tea in the real world.

Overall, Tukoni: Forest Keepers is a fantastic game to play if you're looking for something to get you in the mood for autumn. Its beautiful illustrations will keep you hooked from beginning to end, along with the relaxing gameplay, whether you're simply exploring, interacting with characters, taking in the scenery, solving a puzzle, or enjoying a cup of tea. I had a wonderful time playing this game and it left me feeling really warm, relaxed, and comforted. I would definitely recommend it.

Ultimately, Tukoni: Forest Keepers is a lovely game for anyone looking for something cosy, charming and a little different. Its artwork alone makes it worth experiencing, but there is much more to appreciate beneath those beautiful illustrations. If you’re looking for a peaceful puzzle adventure filled with forest spirits, adorable animals and a little childlike wonder, Tukoni: Forest Keepers is well worth getting lost in.

Tukoni: Forest Keepers is one of those heartwarming cozy games, not only because of the various herbal teas we’ll find ourselves sipping with friends, but also because of the positive vibes that this world and its inhabitants manage to convey. Let’s pause for a moment and let ourselves be carried away like the leaves in a warm and welcoming forest.

While Echoes Of Sekigahara doesn’t quite reach the same narrative heights of the core title, it is nonetheless a wonderful addition, and Most Wanted gives players a refreshing change of pace. Ghost of Yotei: Complete Edition is just that.

Ghost of Yotei Complete Edition is the definitive way to play one of the best games available on PS5, with Echoes of Sekigahara offering a new glimpse into the life of Atsu, and Most Wanted mode offering a new way to enjoy its thrilling combat. If you already own the base game, consider the Complete Edition upgrade a must-have.

Ghost of Yōtei: Complete Edition is chock-full of enjoyable new content that makes an already excellent game even better. The added campaign strengthens the game’s world, while the Most Wanted roguelike mode lets you experience intense combat in a fresh way. There’s no better time or way to experience Sucker Punch’s most recent banger, so I fully recommend giving it a go.

Ghost of Yotei: The Complete Edition is worth your time and attention. Its expansion, Echoes of Sekigahara, adds a strong narrative to the overall body of work, while Most Wanted mode will remind players how much fun the gameplay can be. Combined with additional goodies and a great base game, it is truly a ‘complete’ edition of Atsu’s story.

The obvious question, of course, is whether Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition is worth picking up if you played the original version. And on that front, I’d say it’s a resounding yes. The new story expansion builds on the base game seamlessly, while the Most Wanted mode is great for when you just want to bash away at enemies. Add those on top of a game that was already exceptional, and you can see why it’s worth picking this up.

That’s ultimately what the Complete Edition amounts to: a compact story expansion with one questionable narrative decision, an excellent new single-player mode that’s as satisfying as it is brutal, and a relaxing bonus for anyone who enjoys taking in Ghost of Yōtei’s gorgeous scenery. It’s the definitive way to play Ghost of Yōtei, and it deserves nothing less than the original score I gave it last year.

Echoes of Sekigahara is a content-packed single-player expansion with a riveting story and character writing that elevates the depth of Ghost of Yōtei’s tale of revenge and Atsu’s motivations significantly and has made me appreciate the quality of the base game’s design even more. Even if you aren’t interested in the side modes or unlocks, Sucker Punch’s latest narrative DLC makes the price of admission worth the cost.

Ghost of Yotei Complete Edition takes an already awesome game and adds 2 of the most substantial pieces of DLC I've ever enjoyed as well as oodles of other odds and ends. So, if you love action games then this package is certainly a must-play.

Ghost of Yotei Complete Edition offers a well-rounded package of a great 2025 game. In addition to the excellent updated base game and free multiplayer, there are the new Most Wanted and Echoes of Sekigahara content packs. Most Wanted is just a pastime, aimed at those who have already completed everything in the game and still want to play. Echoes of Sekigahara expands the narrative for a few hours, bringing more details of Atsu's past life. In the end, both DLCs are "more Ghost of Yotei".
Along with Most Wanted and the Legends mode, Echoes of Sekigahara is a great addon, making Ghost of Yotei: Complete Edition feel like a great package.

For their very first game, Wych Elm have blown it out of the park. I recommend Silver Pines to everyone: fans of horror, Metroidvanias, and detective stories. I even encourage those new to those genres to try it out, as it encapsulates a beautifully cinematic experience with a story you’ll want to uncover for yourself.

Silver Pines is a cerebrally divine love letter to David Lynch and all the narrative trademarks he was known for, from the cult classic Twin Peaks to Blue Velvet and Lost Highway. It digs even deeper to its spiritual successor Silent Hill, from the fog-filled streets to the nightmares that lurk with bared teeth, and embraces all those inspirations with the utmost grace and respect while still very much telling its own story. Combat can take a bit to get used to, but feels satisfying after a while with plenty of options at Walker's disposal. Meanwhile, the core investigation aspect of the game is well-executed if a bit unforgiving to the distracted player.

For their very first attempt, Wych Elm have knocked it out of the park. The influences from the masterworks of Lynch, Remedy and Silent Hill, the thriller steeped in ’90s Americana, the discovery of the city’s secrets, and that sense of unease and anticipation about what we’ll encounter every time we step into a new area, blended together in an unforgettable experience.

Silver Pines is a horror search-action game that borrows concepts from established games in the genre and uses them wonderfully to strengthen its own gameplay. The tanky controls and limited inventory kept me anxious as I tried to survive in this abandoned town, while the slowly unravelling story made me doubt whether Red Walker was as sane as he first seemed. The search for Eddie Velvet is a gaming experience that will haunt you like few other PI investigations can.

Compelling, atmospheric, and brilliant, Silver Pines is a dive into mystery that's hard to put down and even harder to let go. It makes you feel like a detective, an action hero, and a man on the brink of uncovering horrifying darkness all at once.

Silver Pines is a great survival-horror that came just at the perfect time. The story is intriguing, the atmosphere is gloomy and creepy, the puzzles are intricate and interesting, and the combat is decent and enjoyable. The minor missed steps with its story and aiming guns are easily forgiven when looking at the bigger picture, and it’s hard not to love it.

Silver Pines is an atmospheric game, a Metroidvania-style survival horror title that draws heavily from genre classics like Silent Hill, Resident Evil, and Alan Wake, as well as from television and film, such as Twin Peaks, The X-Files, and The Shining. However, these inspirations don’t reduce Wych Elm’s work to a mere collection of references; thanks to excellent storytelling, they allow the game to carve out its own path between nightmare and mystery. Solid gameplay underpins the experience, reinterpreting the genre’s conventions without forcing a radical overhaul. It’s also impossible not to mention the excellent art direction, featuring rotoscoped animations, and the soundtrack, with atmospheric music that heightens the tension. Silver Pines is a haunting adventure, a glimpse into the mystery of identity that straddles the line between reality and imagination.

Silver Pines is a glorious revival of the 90s survival horror formula. Fans of the early Silent Hill and Resident Evil games will be thrilled by a title that perfectly distills those classics' formulas, opting for 2D gameplay with strong Metroidvania elements.

Silver Pines is yet another excellent indie horror game and would not be out of place as part of the Silent Hill franchise. The combination of survival horror and more involved platforming exploration works fantastically well, while the town is chock-full of hidden secrets with enigmatic mysteries to solve.

Silver Pines is a sharp, moody debut. It mixes survival horror and Metroidvania design with real confidence. The hand-drawn art is gorgeous. All in all, the atmosphere is thick and unsettling. The mystery pulls you forward, and the world rewards curiosity. Combat feels stiff and lacks satisfaction. The game commits to old-school design. If you love atmospheric horror and don’t mind a slow burn, Silver Pines is a must-play this Halloween season.

reviews.author: MessyStinkman
reviews.quote:
Great atmosphere. The rotoscoped animation looks a lot better in motion than I was expecting it to. The music is excellent, and it effectively builds a good sensation of dread through sound and visual cues while you're exploring.

Combat is not great but not bad either. Enemy variation is severely lacking and you will quickly grow tired of Shambling Guy, Other Shambling Guy, Big Bug and Dog. Controls are a bit clunky and several times I've been hit in ways that feel unfair on a technical level.

Game design is very solid and it is clear they thought very carefully about how you advance. The next tool you find is just barely within reach, and you will use it to create shortcuts and advance further. It definitely scratches the right spots to count as a Metroidvania (even though I really hate that term).

The puzzles are fun and while none so far have really had me scratching my head most have involved a very satisfying loop of item discovery, combination and reference to notes to solve. I especially like that you can take a photo of anything you want to see later, which makes some puzzles, such as remembering a radio's frequency and channel, very simple and they feel good to solve.

Most of the voice acting is top-notch, however I am very much not a fan that they cast an adult movie actor/youtuber as an NPC. Not only does it just conceptually bother me, but this person delivers a flat, sub-par performance. It never really ends well when they do this sort of thing (remember what's his name who was in Cyberpunk? Yeah neither does anyone else) and their performance here really is a D+ at best. Would have been much better off with an unknown.

Still, it can't take away that this is an inspired, thoughtful, and careful game. The people who made this actually cared about it and it shows. It is not the pinnacle of any of the genres it belongs to but it's very good and I'm happy to own it.

Cloudscrapers is a delightful puzzle game that feels exactly the right amount of taxing, and this makes building your fantasy tower such a treat.

The overall design of Cloudscrapers is simple and effective, and I love it. It’s one of many indie games that has grown on me very quickly and will worm its way into most – if not all – of my free time.
Cloudscrapers is just a really nice time that makes you want to come back to it every week or so. It's quick to pick up and understand, but satisfying to truly learn.

Cloudscrapers proves that less is often more, cleverly merging Tetris-style spatial puzzles with tense resource management. Its charming hand-drawn visual style and fast-paced matches deliver an addictive, minimalist loop; however, a forgettable narrative and a lackluster endless mode significantly hurt its long-term replayability once the main campaign concludes.

Lies of P comes closest to capturing FromSoft's signature style, and in some ways, it pushes the genre forward with its innovative weapon-building system and expanded customisation options. The reimagining of a familiar folktale is novel, and the sheer density of content on offer is more than generous. Sometimes it feels like the designers are creating a game that could be their final masterpiece, pouring everything they have into it. Nothing is held back, and every step of the way it surprises with something new.

Lies of P: Complete Edition remains one of the finest soulslikes available, combining methodical combat, rewarding progression, and a compelling reimagining of Pinocchio with the excellent Overture expansion. While the Switch 2 version makes modest visual compromises and experiences occasional frame drops, its strong portable performance and complete package make it an easy recommendation for both newcomers and returning players.

By bundling the base game with the phenomenal Overture expansion, Lies of P: Complete Edition is the ideal way of playing this tremendous soulslike for the first time. There are some caveats, but performance on Switch 2 is largely solid, with multiple graphics settings available to choose from.

One of the best Soulslikes available, Lies of P makes its way to Switch 2 in the form of a Complete Edition. With Performance and Quality modes whether you play handheld or docked, this excellent port means you can now enjoy the base game and its expansion pretty much anywhere you go. And thanks to its post-launch support, which includes difficulty options, this is a must-have for action RPG fans.

I absolutely adore Lies of P. I foolishly ignored it back in 2023 because I thought it would be just yet another Dark Souls clone. But while it certainly borrows heavily from FromSoftware's catalogue, it does more than enough to stand on its own two feet with exceptional world design, awesome boss characters, and a wonderfully customisable weapon system. Performance isn't perfect on Switch 2, and I wouldn't recommend playing in Quality mode, but experiencing Lies of P on the go has been an absolute blast. FromSoftware better watch its back; there's a new player in town, and it's gunning for the Soulslike crown.
Lies of P Complete Edition performs wonderfully on the Nintendo Switch 2, inviting both new and existing players to experience the story of Pinocchio in a unique and exciting way.

Lies of P: Complete Edition on the Nintendo Switch 2 is a standout port of an already beautifully-designed game. From its graphical options to its full collection of DLC, it’s a worthy contender. This is especially true if you’ve never played a soulslike before – this is one you shouldn’t skip.

Lies of P: Complete Edition was a delightful experience. Considering that this is this team’s first shot at a big console single-player release, I’m blown away that I was left thinking it was probably the best Souls game I’ve ever played. It’s good in ways that don’t have me dismissive of the rest of the genre, but instead have me wanting to tackle all of them from a new perspective. I want to go back and appreciate all of the FromSoftware games I never finished, since now I know exactly what parts of the game design I value. If you’ve never played a Souls game, I think this is a great entry point. The difficulty curve might dissuade enthusiasts, but if they stick with it, I think even they’ll find themselves rewarded by the end with wonderfully difficult fights. There’s something for everyone here, and if Overture is anything to go by, they know what they do well. I don’t think I’ve been more excited for an upcoming sequel in a really long time.

Lies of P remains one of the best non-FromSoftware soulslikes - atmospheric, challenging, and rewarding. Although balance changes and level linearity take some of the shine off, the game still delivers a strong experience, and the Switch 2 port is surprisingly solid.

Lies of P is a great Souls like game. If you didn’t get a chance to pick it up when it first came out, give it a chance here. If you do own it and want a way to bring it on the go, again you can’t really go wrong.  I must not tell lies; Lies of P is worth your time and money!

If Xenoblade Chronicles 2 were a Blade, the original Switch was its Driver one that couldn’t maximize its potential. Thanks to the Switch 2 update and its technical and gameplay improvements, it finally has the Driver it deserves.

Xenoblade Chronicles 2 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition is everything I wanted out of an upgrade, with sharper visuals, 60 FPS performance, and one of the original game's biggest frustrations finally fixed. More than anything, it gave me an excuse to return to Alrest and experience one of my favorite games of all time in the best way possible. Nearly nine years later, Xenoblade Chronicles 2 remains an unforgettable RPG that stands among the very best games I have ever played.

When it launched in 2017, Xenoblade Chronicles 2 was too ambitious for the Nintendo Switch hardware (and Nintendo knew it). Its story—filled with memorable cutscenes—its engaging characters, and its massive world (which makes the player feel like an ant amidst the vastness of the colossi) can now finally be enjoyed with the quality they always deserved.
Xenoblade Chronicles 2 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition makes an all time great even better, and there's never been a better time to jump in.

Over time (and at least one additional replay) I’ve become more comfortable with the tonal dissonance beating at the heart of XC2. And it’s not like I was ever unhappy with either the fan service or the serious narrative. It was just the juxtaposition that threw me at the time. So, while this might not be my favourite title in the overall series, I do think it is magnificent, and all the better now we can see the creative vision that the developers had for it in the first place.

Xenoblade Chronicles 2 is an essential JRPG, and on Switch 2 it finally feels like it’s reached its ultimate form with upscaling that massively improves clarity and performance, and some light bits of added content alongside.

Xenoblade Chronicles 2 Nintendo Switch 2 Edition had the biggest job to do of any of these updates, thanks to the age of the original Switch release. Thankfully, it mostly hits the mark. There are still a few graphical issues that keep it from being all it could be, but it’s hard to argue that this isn’t a clear and obvious upgrade in most ways that count. It features smoother framerates, improved resolution, more visual details, some genuinely useful quality of life upgrades, and even has some new content to check out. If you want to cruise the clouds of Alrest in style, this one’s well-worth picking up.

Xenoblade Chronicles 2 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition brings the audiovisual treatment and performance that this absolutely epic RPG more than deserved, and adds a number of very welcome changes concerning the Field Skills, as well as the new Merc Assault. For those who own the original version, this update is more than worth the effort, whereas new players will find themselves at awe with the staggering amount of exploration to do and the enormous world unfurling in front of their eyes.

You’ve likely played Xenoblade or know what to expect at this point. The bottom line is that if Xenoblade Chronicles 2 was already a must-play almost a decade ago, you’re doing yourself a disservice by not having this in your Switch 2 collection in 2026.
Xenoblade Chronicles 2 arrives on Nintendo Switch 2 in the version it always deserved: sharp, smooth, and enhanced with a few extras that round out the experience.

Planet Zoo 2 raises the bar for the simulation genre, with new features and quality-of-life tweaks making the latest Frontier Developments title not only as the kings of the jungle, but also conquerors of the sea and the air.
Most importantly, every creature feels well-designed and well-thought-out. They don’t behave the same, and I lost so many hours simply observing what my favorite inhabitants were up to.

With lovely visual upgrades to its sprawling roster of land, air, and sea-dwelling animals and exciting expanded mechanics, Planet Zoo 2 is a vibrant and thriving sequel. I wasn't absolutely awed by all of the new stuff, and in particular I think wildlife reserves could be a lot richer than they are. But with plenty of management features to challenge my strategy-loving side and endlessly flexible building tools to inspire my creative side, there's not a lot more I could ask for. It's a roaring success.
Planet Zoo 2 isn’t a revolution, but it doesn’t need to be. It takes what made the original great and improves upon it in every way.

It's safe to say that Planet Zoo 2 is Frontier's biggest and best game yet. It looks fantastic, has a huge range of animals, and its greater focus on conservation makes for a wholesome and rewarding experience. There's a learning curve involved, though, so be prepared to put in the time if you want to get the most out of this wonderful sim.

Planet Zoo 2 is a stupendous upgrade over Frontier's first effort from 2019. The improvements made to the animal AI pathing, zoo customization and the new habitats areastounding. Frontier has made tremendous strides in this sequel, and while it may feel overwhelming to new players even with its comprehensive story mode, it may be a bit too much all at once in some places. That being said, absolutely nothing should stop you from taking the plunge into this spectacular zoo management simulation.

Planet Zoo 2 is, in my opinion, one of the best management sims ever made. The level of detail in not just the animals, but also the technical details and real-world education provided is like no other. It's so easy to lose yourself in a zoo, creating the perfect habitats for the amazing animals and truly feeling responsible for them and their well-being. The addition of aviaries and aquariums is a welcome one, and it's incredibly enjoyable to have the option to turn off the UI, go into a cinematic mode and simply watch the animals do their thing.
The fantastic aquariums and aviaries make Planet Zoo 2 the ultimate zoo simulator, though quite a few animals from multiple continents are still needed to make that dream complete.

Planet Zoo 2 is an engaging and rewarding management sim with gorgeous animal models and animations, alongside remarkable creative freedom. Despite a few shortcomings, some of which it has inherited from its predecessor, it is an excellent choice for players who love detailed management, though those primarily seeking a relaxing experience with animals may find it overwhelming.
Quotation forthcoming.

What surprised me most about Allogloom is how much it reminded me of the point-and-click games I played when I was younger, without ever feeling childish. A straight line runs from the curiosity that made me click everything in Putt-Putt, Pajama Sam, or Freddi Fish to the curiosity that kept pulling me deeper into Gruesome Grove and the world around it. The difference is what waits on the other side of the click. Those childhood games rewarded curiosity with jokes, animations, and friendly characters; Allogloom sometimes rewards it with something you probably wish you didn’t know, and I mean that as a compliment. Perhaps that’s why the comparison to those childhood adventures feels so correct. Allogloom feels like the genre grew up alongside the people who played them. The curiosity is still there, as are the strange characters and the inventory full of seemingly useless nonsense, but the questions are different now, and the answers can be considerably more uncomfortable. It reminded me why I used to click on absolutely everything in Putt-Putt, Pajama Sam, and Freddi Fish, without ever wanting to replay any of those games. We’re older now, and the moths grew up with us. Allogloom is definitely one of those point-and-click games I’ll recommend for years to come.
Allogloom is a beautiful, short game with an amazing, twisted art style, deep lore, and simple yet fun puzzles.

For those who want a neatly packaged, slightly eerie, yet beautiful escape to another world, Allogloom is amazing. If anything, I wish I could’ve had just a little bit more about the spaces we visit to see what was happening in each area. Again, this isn’t anything that’s a true negative, but I did end up with just a few questions on some of the areas we find ourselves. I want to learn more about the settings that have been created for Nora. The areas she finds herself in all seem to have their own reasons for being and I’d want just a little more to understand why. But even without this, Allogloom is a game worth your time if you want a bit of horror with your point and click games.
A macabre take on other worlds and how one perceives reality, Allogloom is a creepy-cute point-and-click treat for fans of haunting tales.

In its logic strings, Aloogloom is so satisfying. There’s victory in discovering exactly which item works with another, and that’s what all good point-and-click adventures should aspire to achieve. Pair this system with Allogloom‘s lush, moody artwork and its layered, macabre themes, and it’s an entirely unique experience that is rich and beautiful in approach. It’s a very strong debut from developer Galactic Ghosty, and one that deserves your attention.

After a long hiatus, Castlevania is back and better than ever. Konami's trust in Evil Empire as the stewards of a new 2D era has been well-placed, with a modern and fresh-feeling take that builds on what's always made the series so iconic while carving out its own identity. Rose Belmont is a fantastic protagonist that lends Belmont's Curse a compelling story and heightened exploration. This is an instant classic.

A bold evolution that redefines the future of the franchise, Belmont’s Curse delivers the finest exploration and gameplay systems in Castlevania’s history, setting a new standard for this legendary IP.

Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse is an amazing return to the series’ 2D roots. By blending tight combat and fluid controls, satisfying mechanics via Sypha’s Tarot cards and relics, and punishing platforming, Evil Empire has crafted a Metroidvania experience that honors the franchise’s legacy while also creating its own identity.

The Castlevania series is one that’s near and dear to my heart. I’ve spent decades playing these games since the very first one, and the balance that Belmont’s Curse strikes between being an incredible platforming adventure all on its own and respecting the series’ myriad directions and gimmicks, good and bad, was impressive start to finish. Stellar gameplay, music, scenery, characters (new and old), and a great set of options for altering the intensity make this the easily one of the highest-quality action-platformers I have ever played. When the dust settles, I think there’s a case to be made that Belmont’s Curse might be the best Castlevania game of all time.

Exceptional in every way, Castlevania: Belmont's Curse is a one of 2026's must-play titles. In a year of great games, it's hard to stand out, but Evil Empire has crafted a bonified masterpiece in one of the game's most historic franchises.

Castlevania: Belmont's Curse is not just one of the best games this year; it's one of the best Castlevania games ever made. It is a challenging, consistently engaging, and superbly designed adventure epic that reminds us why this series defined an entire genre in the first place.

None of the tiny qualms I’ve listed mar the fact that Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse is an incredible experience from start to finish. It looks, sounds, reads, and plays with sleek style, while asking a thoughtfulness of the player not typically seen in this genre. Taken alone in another game, any of this game’s elements would stand out. The fact that every element blends so perfectly here makes me confident to say that Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse is the best Metroidvania I’ve ever experienced. It’s sure to go down as an all-time classic.

Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse is an absolute dream come true for everyone who loves this series. I can’t believe what Evil Empire, Motion Twin, and Konami are bringing to the table. It’s almost as if we, the fans, had sat down and simply asked for everything we wanted to see in a new 2D Castlevania game in 2026. It’s hard to find any significant flaws in this game, which pushes the genre that the series itself helped define to new heights, making it clear that its importance goes far beyond the historical contributions we’ve talked about so much. The return of the Belmonts is more than just a triumph for the legendary Japanese publisher; it’s a celebration of everything that makes our beloved video games so special.

With a storied past, Castlevania: Belmont's Curse sets up the franchise for a bright (but also dark) future. Rose is a fantastic heroine with a deep, compelling story, and she wields some of the genre's most enjoyable combat mechanics. Add a few key accessibility options to make the game less punishing, and I think you have a standout title heading into the final months of 2026. Belmont's Curse is one of the best ways Konami and Evil Empire could have pushed the franchise and the genre forward.

Castlevania: Belmont's Curse masterfully marks the return of the franchise by delivering the finest Metroidvania experience since Symphony of the Night. Combining a narrative that honors the Belmont family legacy with an innovative Tarot card skill-absorption system and a striking art style, the title overcomes minor mechanical flaws to establish itself as the start of a promising future for the series.
Monolith did some fine work with these two games, and these Switch 2 ports give a new audience the chance to experience the enduring magic of the Nemesis System.
Playing both Shadow of Mordor and Shadow of War, it's incredible that the free-flow combat paired with the Nemesis system still hits so hard.

Revisiting Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor on Switch 2 has been an absolute joy. I’d forgotten just how incredible that visceral combat feels, but more importantly… just how fascinating the Nemesis System is. Could it have benefited from a framerate boost? Absolutely. A game this good running at 60fps would have been fantastic, and there are moments where the 30fps cap is noticeable. But that never stopped me from getting completely immersed in Mordor. Aspyr has brought across an outstanding game that, despite being more than a decade old, still manages to stand toe-to-toe with much more modern titles. While I may not know enough about the wider lore of The Lord of the Rings, this was one story I just couldn’t put down.

Two great adventures that you can now relive anywhere thanks to this ports which, although they get almost everything right, do have a few bugs that can be fixed via a patch. That said, there are no new features – neither technical nor gameplay-related – nor any that take advantage of the Switch 2’s capabilities, they are the same games that we played on PS4, PC and Xbox One.
The two main entries of the Middle Earth series arrive on Switch 2 to surprise us with two solid adventures that still manage to feel fresh and fun thanks to its Nemesis system.

Middle-earth: Shadow Bundle is a solid compilation of one of the best game adaptations set in Tolkien's world. While visually comparable to the PS4 and Xbox One versions, it remains a worthwhile purchase for Nintendo fans.

Lords of the End Times is an expansion focused entirely on its protagonists, all of whom are undeniably well-realized. Thanquol is perhaps the most intriguing, thanks to his grand schemes and risk-taking nature, while Boris Todbringer answers the community’s long-standing requests. Nagash and the Glottkin round out a quartet that feels perfectly suited to this apocalyptic setting. Ultimately, the DLC’s value lies in the sheer volume of content Creative Assembly has prepared for us. And when an expansion makes us look at *Immortal Empires* with the feeling that there is still something new to discover, it means Total War: WARHAMMER III undoubtedly still has a few cards—and turns—left to play.

Lords of the End Times adds a substantial amount of excellent content to an already massive game. Thanks to the new and powerful Legendary Lords and the Devastation System, Total War: Warhammer III feels fresh again. Aside from some balancing issues and Boris Todbringer’s slightly lackluster campaign, Warhammer III, Lords of the End Times is both must-have content for longtime fans and a great place to jump in to an already excellent strategy game.
Lord of the End Times finally brings some of the biggest fan favorites into the game—and does them justice in the process.

That said, it is clear that they do not revolutionize anything—nor do they claim to; they simply aim to add value to a game world whose core characteristics are already well-established. This is evident from a technical standpoint as well, given the meticulous attention to detail across all four packs—from flawlessly animated units and high-quality static artwork and cinematics to new, dedicated musical scores. In short, if you have already played *Total War: Warhammer III* and want to return to it, this is an excellent way to do so; conversely, if you haven't played it yet but are interested in these four factions, you now have a fantastic entry point into what is currently one of the best strategy games on the market.

reviews.author: Geek_and_Chill
reviews.quote:
Conclusion: Nagash Finally Takes His Rightful Place
Lords of the End Times deserves its place among the most interesting additions to Total War: WARHAMMER III. Nagash offers an ambitious campaign that ties his rise to power to the development of an entire undead empire. Thanquol transforms Skaven cunning into fun and useful decisions. The Glottkin complement the Chaos Warriors well, and Boris gives Middenland its own army and objectives. The expansion pack thus offers much more than just four characters to slot into unchanged campaigns.
The package remains uneven, with Boris being significantly more conventional and the Glottkin feeling less novel to Chaos veterans. The power of the new lords also widens the gap with the old ones, while the bugs that still remain and the clunkiness of certain systems prevent one from accepting everything unreservedly. The free update significantly improves the context, but it shouldn’t be used to inflate the DLC’s value. As for the purchase itself, Nagash and Thanquol are the two top priorities; the full pack is most worthwhile for those who actually plan to play all four campaigns.

Highlights   
Nagash’s campaign and his recruitment system, which brings together the three undead traditions    
Thanquol’s Grand Schemes, which truly integrate intrigue into strategy    Distinct armies and objectives for the four lords    
New units that enrich army compositions    
Access to Immortal Empires available with a single €8.99 pack

Cons    
Boris’s campaign is less inventive, despite having the same price per character    The Glottkins offer less of a change of pace for those familiar with the Chaos Warriors    
Power and richness that highlight the gap between them and former lords    
Systems and an interface that are still intimidating for new players    
Quest issues and problems accessing the Bone Giant still present in version 9.0.2
