It's a game with no personality, probably thrown together by teenage developers using AI. It feels cheap and hollow, like it's made of paper and empty on the inside.

The passion behind Nighthawks is evident in every delicious drop of dialogue and heartfelt character moment throughout its impressive runtime. It’s the kind of game that will sink its teeth into you with its addictive RPG mechanics and mesmerize you into staying up way past your bedtime.

Kickstarted back in 2018, it may have taken eight years for Nighthawks to crawl out of its coffin, but it was worth the wait. Enthralling, entertaining and with rich, razor-sharp writing, if you have even the slightest interest in vampires or the supernatural, you'll want to sink your teeth into this gothic gem.
If you're not put off by reading a lot of words then here's a well-written vampire chronicle.

Nighthawks is a delightful experience for anyone who likes stories and vampires. The setting, with its three big neighborhoods and human-vampire interactions, is familiar, but the narrative threads feature plenty of surprises and cool characters. I like most of the companions, and one of the best parts of the game is discovering how they react to each location and how they interact with new characters. The attention to narrative detail is commendable, but it cannot fully mask the relatively limited gameplay. Players move around and talk most of the time. Combat is very limited, and results can feel arbitrary. Nighthawks can be too ambitious for its own good, but it has the atmosphere and story moments to keep gamers interested in its bloody world.
A notable narrative effort with an interesting setting, great writing and outstanding vocal work, but lacking on the RPG elements.

Nighthawks has plenty about it, including a number of excellent side stories, but is dragged down by RPG mechanics that didn't do enough to make me properly commit to the idea of role-playing my vampire. I felt like I couldn't immerse myself in my character, and so I became detached with what was happening in the city. Some of the narrative and story decisions would have hit harder if my character was developing at the same time, and it's a shame that the potential hasn't been fully realised.

These problems spin together and mean Nighthawks as a whole never quite comes into focus. The couple at the counter are painted in exquisite detail, and at times I feel I’m inside the warm diner, perhaps even brushing hands with a loved one. But the rest of the picture doesn’t evoke the loneliness that casts these moments in sharp relief. Instead of deliberate emptiness, it feels like an uneven sketch.

A gentle diorama puzzle adventure invites players to assemble charming wooden scenes piece by piece while following a warm, nostalgic story. Its relaxing pace and cozy atmosphere make it an easy game to unwind with. I wood recommend this game to everyone.
While its construction and play are relatively simple, cozy, and satisfying, I also appreciate some smart design that shows an earnest effort on the part of the developers.

I am well aware that we are right in the middle of one of the busiest periods in video game history, but I can’t recommend Woodo enough. It’s a short, beautiful game, both visually and narratively, filled with adorable characters and stunning dioramas that are incredibly satisfying to piece back together. It’s a terrific first game from Tiny Monks Tales, and if the plan is to develop more games with similar vibes to Woodo, then I will be there day one for whatever comes next.

By combining different facets of an assortment of peaceful activities — colouring-in, jigsaw-puzzling, Lego-building and more — Woodo hits on a formula for pure relaxation. Its gorgeous presentation, both graphics and sound, makes it irresistible to interact with. There’s a lot of repetition involved in getting into the zone, and sometimes I wished the storytelling would get out of the way and lean into the unspoken feelings that the dioramas convey without a voiceover. However, none of that was enough to snap me out of its cosy spell.

Woodo is a storybook puzzle game that aims to be as comfortable as a good flannel on a chill autumn day. And it succeeds. It also ends before the puzzle dynamic wears out its welcome, and will elicit enough smiles to keep cozy game fans entertained throughout.

Woodo is a warm blanket - a puzzle experience for players of all ages that tries to shake up the formula despite its simple structure. Just be aware that it is a 3–4 hour adventure with little replay value, and the camera can sometimes get confused between the object you are trying to focus on and the rest of the diorama.

reviews.author: GhostArrow
reviews.quote:
Building up your duelists, finding better gear, crafting upgrades, and taking on bosses makes progression satisfying.

One thing worth mentioning is that this isn't a completely hands-off idle game. You'll spend quite a bit of time managing your inventory, selling unwanted gear, upgrading your team, and preparing for boss fights. Personally, I don't see that as a downside, but if you're looking for a game that practically plays itself in the background, this might not be what you expect.

If you enjoy idle games with a bit more hands-on progression, there's a lot to like here.

Mafia: The Old Country - Man of Honor might be more of the same, and that’s perfectly okay with me. Hangar 13’s nod to the original game is appreciated, as is the narrative flair The Old Country has already. Seeing Free Ride revamped is also a pleasure, alongside a meaty amount of content via Salieri’s introduction to the map. Sure, the gameplay doesn’t see a similar update, and your weapons and vehicles are in the same boat, but this might be the best $10 expansion you could spend money on.

Mafia The Old Country Man of Honor gives fans of the base game a compelling reason to return to Sicily, delivering an engaging new story that fits seamlessly into the established narrative alongside additional activities that make its open world feel more meaningful. While the core gameplay remains largely unchanged and is unlikely to win over new players, the expansion effectively reminds longtime fans exactly what made the original experience so appealing.

Mafia: The Old Country – Man of Honor is a DLC that doesn’t aim to introduce new gameplay elements to the original game; rather, it’s more of the same, offering a narrative episode set during the main story, not after it ends. The new story, starring Enzo, lasts about two hours, and it’s precisely this short playtime that might deter many players, given the €9.99 price tag for the additional content. On the other hand, there are excellent new additions to the “Free Ride” mode, with missions that let you return to the Sicilian countryside and fully enjoy the scenery created by Hangar 13, scenery we loved so much in the base game released a year ago.

For anyone who has finished the main campaign and is hungry for more criminal action, Man of Honor is well worth its $10 USD price tag. Even though the main story wraps up in roughly three hours—depending on whether you prefer a slow, methodical stealth approach or an explosive firefight—the addition of Free Ride activities and collection goals rounds out a solid package.
Man of Honor doesn’t reinvent The Old Country, but its compact story, stronger Free Ride content and connections to the wider series make it a worthwhile return.

Man of Honor works best when it places Enzo next to a Salieri who has already learned how easily a code of honor can bend to personal ambition, creating a meaningful bridge to the first Mafia. The problem is that two hours are barely enough to develop that contrast, while stealth and combat inherit most of The Old Country’s weaknesses unchanged. Free Ride gains better context and more purposeful activities, but some of its content still feels checklist-driven. A solid DLC, but too brief and conservative to rise above.

Man of Honor works well as a small expansion to the story of Mafia: The Old Country. However, while it retains the essence of the base game and offers a great atmosphere, it falls short in terms of depth.

The Man of Honor DLC expansion recognizes that Mafia stories aren't really about guns, cars or crime. They're about loyalty, ambition, betrayal and the price people are willing to pay to be part of something bigger than themselves.
2K is wrapping up content for Mafia: The Old Country with an expansion that, while shorter, is interesting for fans. It also adds an update that expands the range of activities.

A Wild West atmosphere, monsters, and immense Polish creativity come together in this addictive title featuring tactical combat. However, the game is challenging and becomes repetitive over time.

Nightmare Frontier is an interesting tactical game, and its blend with roguelites increases the replay value, while also adding a great twist. Plus, it is an extraction game as well, and the ability to extract whenever you want or risk it all for a more difficult encounter does keep you on the edge. It’s certainly a game for strategy enthusiasts and tactics experts, but I think it’s not as complex as some of the genre’s greats. That helps increase accessibility, while still offering plenty of gameplay ideas for you to explore. One of the strengths of Nightmare Frontier is the fact that it’s addictive, immersive and intense. I felt that some of the locations repeat quite often, so even if the gameplay is good, the repetitive aspect of a roguelite brings things down a little bit. It also doesn’t help that some of the enemies are repeating pretty often. But once you get past that, the game is excellent, it does a great job for what it tries to achieve, although I hope more content such as new maps will be added in the future.
Nightmare Frontier achieves something that is increasingly rare: carving out its own identity in a genre as crowded as turn-based tactical strategy.
Clever turn-based tactics with intense but fair battles. Not much fluff, and the quirky story is presented only in text form.

Under different circumstances, one might say that these stumbling blocks could be ironed out over time, but one cannot overlook the game's long stint in early access. Ultimately, it is a solid turn-based tactical game that employs a fully deterministic system, turning every phase of battle into a mini-puzzle to be solved using the tools at hand. Yet, while the integration of extraction-genre elements and the customization system rest on very solid foundations, they also contend with a certain repetitiveness and formulaic nature; combined with slow progression, these issues risk making the experience feel overly mechanical and drawn-out. The core concept is sound and works well, but truly rounding out the experience would have required greater variety, more depth, and perhaps a bit more attention to the interplay between narrative and gameplay—qualities that likely lay beyond the scope of the studio's ambitions.

Nightmare Frontier does its part, between novelties and good ideas, unfortunately the latter run out quickly and the rest is a good filler, but certainly less interesting than the first hours. Certainly the seeds of a structure that deserves a posthumous study have been planted. [Early Access Review Score = 70]

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its engaging co-op gameplay, unique puzzle design, and the emotional connection it fosters among friends. Many found it to be a refreshing and memorable experience, with some even considering it the best co-op game they've played. However, some noted that the game could be tedious with slow movement and lacked replay value for solo play.
summaries.dislikes: Critics pointed out the game's slow pace and large map, which can be tedious to navigate. Some also found the puzzles to be uneven in quality, with some being more enjoyable than others. Additionally, a few reviewers felt the game was overpriced or not entertaining enough when played with acquaintances or strangers.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its outstanding combat, compelling narrative, and strong cast. They also highlighted the quality of life improvements and the overall masterful remake that enhances the original.
summaries.dislikes: Some critics noted that the game's pacing could be improved, with some sections feeling slow or dragging. Additionally, a few mentioned that the supporting material and some dungeons felt underdeveloped or repetitive.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its deep and rewarding combat system, richly developed characters, and emotionally impactful storytelling. The modern presentation and improvements over the original were also highly appreciated, with many considering it a must-play for JRPG fans.
summaries.dislikes: Some reviewers noted that the pacing could occasionally feel slow, particularly when tracking down specific objectives or completing obscure side quests. Additionally, a few mentioned that the soundtrack, while generally praised, could be improved, especially with the work of a particular composer.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the Elden Ring Tarnished Edition for its near-perfect port, excellent performance on the Switch 2, and the ability to fully enjoy the game's open-world experience in handheld mode. They also highlighted the inclusion of the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion and the game's captivating nature.
summaries.dislikes: Some critics noted minor technical flaws and occasional performance dips, but these were generally considered minor issues that did not significantly impact the overall experience. The Switch 2 port was also noted to be slightly less detailed compared to the PlayStation 5 version, but this was deemed a minor difference.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game's visuals, optimization, and the ability to play it on the go. They also appreciated the substantial content and the new classes and weapons added in the Tarnished Edition.
summaries.dislikes: Some found the game's frame rate and performance issues on the Switch 2 to be a significant drawback, while others felt the game was not as enjoyable as expected and lacked polish compared to other Souls-like games.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game's deep and rewarding gameplay, its tactile artillery mechanics, and the immersive experience. They also highlighted the game's unique setting and the strategic depth it offers.
summaries.dislikes: Some found the initial learning curve challenging, and while the narrative was appreciated as a thematic framework, it was not as engaging as a character-driven story. The game's length was also noted as a potential drawback for some players.

summaries.likes: Some reviewers appreciated the novelty of each mission and the satisfying gameplay mechanics. The campaign was seen as well-balanced with the right challenge level.
summaries.dislikes: Many found the game tedious and repetitive, with unclear aiming targets and stressful timed missions. The lack of visibility for the player was a significant criticism, along with concerns about potential plagiarism.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised Enshrouded for its impressive survival and crafting mechanics, atmospheric open world, and versatile building system. It also offers a good balance between solo and multiplayer gameplay, making it appealing to a wide range of players.
summaries.dislikes: Some critics noted that the combat lacks depth and the voxel-based world has limitations, while others found the game to be slightly less innovative compared to its peers in the genre.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised Well Dweller for its polished gameplay, engaging exploration, and charming design, with many noting its appeal to both newcomers and veterans of the Metroidvania genre. The game's atmosphere, storytelling, and movement mechanics were also highly appreciated.
summaries.dislikes: Some found the combat repetitive and the difficulty curve too gentle for experienced players, while others felt the game could have better utilized its level design potential. However, these critiques were generally outweighed by the positive feedback.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its unique movement abilities, engaging story, and beautiful art style, with some calling it a masterpiece and a top game of the year. The gameplay was also highly appreciated, with fun puzzles and challenging bosses.
summaries.dislikes: Some found the game a bit too easy, with bosses becoming trivial to defeat, and criticized the repetitive nature of combat mechanics. The game's progression felt somewhat predictable, with some puzzles and challenges feeling by-the-numbers.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its ambitious and engaging storyline, deep strategic gameplay, and well-written characters. They also highlighted the impressive pacing and the unique twists in each hero's story path.
summaries.dislikes: Some critics noted minor presentational issues and slight imbalances in the Overblaze system, but these were seen as minor drawbacks in an otherwise exceptional game.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game's engaging stories, diverse gameplay, and deep tactical depth, especially in Part 1 and Part 3. They also appreciated the music and character designs.
summaries.dislikes: Critics found the game's sci-fi theme and time-travel mechanics clashing with the traditional Fire Emblem formula, leading to a disjointed experience. They also criticized the game's balance issues, particularly the RNG system and the abundance of downtime activities.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised Valheim for its stunning visuals, engaging gameplay, and the sense of discovery and exploration. They also highlighted the game's rich crafting and base-building mechanics, as well as its community engagement and replayability.
summaries.dislikes: Some critics noted minor issues with player comfort and a few procedural generation pitfalls, but these were seen as minor compared to the game's overall quality and success.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised Valheim for its engaging gameplay, unique building mechanics, and immersive world exploration. The game was also commended for its lack of microtransactions and the satisfaction derived from crafting and base building.
summaries.dislikes: Critics found the game tedious and grindy, particularly in the mid-to-late game, with issues like clunky combat and restrictive metal hauling. Some also criticized the game's difficulty and the lack of a more forgiving mode, as well as the need for mods to address various bugs and balance issues.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised Fields of Mistria for its exceptional gameplay, charming characters, and polished design, with some noting its potential to rival Stardew Valley. Many found the game's narrative and RPG elements well-integrated, and its visual style to be particularly appealing.
summaries.dislikes: A few critics noted minor issues such as lag, combat and resource RNG imbalances, and the game's early release stage, which included some unfinished elements. However, these were generally outweighed by the game's strengths.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its comprehensive gameplay, rewarding activities, and customizable features. They also appreciated the engaging characters and the game's affordability.
summaries.dislikes: Some found the 90 anime art style less appealing, and a few wished for more personality in the datable characters. Additionally, one reviewer preferred another game over Fields of Mistria.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised Bubbly Basin for its extensive content, new areas, and Pokémon, as well as its adherence to the established formula while offering new exploration and features. Critics also highlighted the calming exploration, new biome, and the ability to spend hours playing.
summaries.dislikes: Some reviewers noted that the story missions lacked detail, and the game might not appeal to those not already invested in the base game. Additionally, the decision to set the entire game underwater was seen as a limitation for some.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the extensive content, quality of life features, and overall quality of the game, considering it a must-play for fans of the series. They also highlighted the addictive gameplay and the addition of new secrets and features in the DLC.
summaries.dislikes: Critics noted the low score of 10/100, which might indicate issues with the game's technical aspects or the scoring system itself. However, no specific dislikes were mentioned regarding gameplay or content.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised Welcome to Elderfield for its unique blend of horror and farming simulation, its well-crafted narrative and atmosphere, and the engaging gameplay that keeps players hooked. It was also noted for its distinctive art direction and the depth of its world, which offers plenty of secrets and mysteries to uncover.
summaries.dislikes: Some critics found the game's progression and explanation of certain elements to be unclear, and a few mentioned minor bugs. However, these issues were seen as minor compared to the game's overall quality and originality.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game's unique blend of farming, survival horror, and RPG elements, its atmospheric and cozy setting, and the unexpected and interesting events that keep the gameplay engaging. They also appreciated the attention to detail in world-building and the use of RPG Maker to create a game that feels both familiar and fresh.
summaries.dislikes: Some reviewers found the game to be unfairly difficult, particularly with the rat encounters, and wished for accessibility features like colorblind filters. A few noted that the game might not be as exciting for those who have played similar titles, but still highly recommended it for its unique take on the genre.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game's beautiful illustrations, charming characters, and peaceful gameplay. They also appreciated the game's cozy atmosphere and the variety of puzzles and interactions.
summaries.dislikes: Some found the game too short, while others noted that the main character, Traveller, was not a big personality. However, the game's positive vibes and wholesome interactions were generally well-received.

summaries.likes: Both reviewers praised the game's art style and the engaging puzzles. They also appreciated the wholesome storyline and the adaptation for controllers.
summaries.dislikes: However, both gave it the lowest possible score, suggesting significant issues with the game's mechanics or overall experience that outweighed its positive aspects.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the Complete Edition for its excellent narrative expansion, 'Echoes of Sekigahara', which adds depth to the story, and the 'Most Wanted' mode, which offers a fresh combat experience. The base game was also highly commended for its quality and aesthetics.
summaries.dislikes: A few critics noted that 'Echoes of Sekigahara' had a questionable narrative decision, and that 'Most Wanted' was more of a pastime for those who had already completed the main game. However, these were minor criticisms in the context of the overall positive reception.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the gameplay, especially the Most Wanted mode and DLC, which they found added depth and enjoyment to the game. They also appreciated the artistic direction and soundtrack.
summaries.dislikes: Many found the protagonist lacking in depth and charisma, similar to previous criticisms of the game. Some also noted repetitive gameplay and a story that didn't meet their expectations.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its delightful and challenging puzzle gameplay, simple yet effective design, and quick-to-understand mechanics that offer long-term satisfaction. The charming visual style and addictive loop were also highlighted.
summaries.dislikes: Critics noted a forgettable narrative and lackluster endless mode as drawbacks, which affected the game's long-term replayability. Some found the main campaign to be taxing but not sufficiently engaging for repeated playthroughs.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised Lies of P: Complete Edition for its innovative weapon-building system, compelling reimagining of Pinocchio, and the overall quality of the game, making it one of the best soulslikes available. They also highlighted the complete package, including the Overture expansion and multiple performance modes.
summaries.dislikes: Some critics noted that performance on Switch 2 was not perfect, with occasional frame drops in Quality mode, and balance changes and level linearity issues that slightly impacted the experience.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game's storytelling, combat mechanics, and overall gameplay, comparing it favorably to FromSoftware titles and Bloodborne. They also highlighted the game's optimization for the Nintendo Switch 2, its portable play, and the completeness of the Complete Edition.
summaries.dislikes: Some reviewers noted minor issues such as graphical compromises in handheld mode and the game's score being unusually low, possibly due to a typo or misunderstanding.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the upgrade for its improved visuals, smoother performance, and enhanced gameplay, making the game feel like its ultimate form. They also highlighted the addition of new content and the resolution of long-standing issues.
summaries.dislikes: Some critics noted minor graphical issues and that the upgrade wasn't perfect, with a few areas still needing improvement. However, they agreed that the overall experience was significantly better and well worth the update.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game's story, characters, and combat system, with many noting the improvements in graphics and performance. They also highlighted the game's world and soundtrack as major strengths.

summaries.likes: The reviewer appreciates the DLCs as essential to the game's core experience, emphasizing the free updates and additions that enhance the gameplay without the need for additional purchases.

summaries.likes: The game's progression from basic to more creative tasks is praised, as well as the story that unlocks more creative assignments.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its exceptional combat system, deep and challenging gameplay, and the rich, immersive world of feudal Japan. They also highlighted the strong performances, memorable characters, and the overall quality of the game.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the combat system, describing it as solid, engaging, and satisfying. They also appreciated the game's aesthetic and the blend of traditional Japanese feudalism with dark fantasy elements.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game's strategic depth, unique specializations, and engaging story, especially for Star Wars fans. The tactical combat and character customization were also highlighted as strong points.

Some found the difficulty level to be too easy, and the game's reliance on mechanics from other titles without proper integration was a letdown.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised Sovereign Tower for its engaging time-travel mechanic, deep management systems, and rich narrative, with many noting the game's ability to balance tragedy and comedy. The game's charming characters and Arthurian setting also received positive attention.

The game's complexity and pacing were also cited as potential drawbacks for some players.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its deep narrative, branching choices, and engaging time rewind mechanic. They also appreciated the charming art style, memorable characters, and the ability to relive and change outcomes.
summaries.dislikes: Some found the latter part of the game too simple once the knights were well-trained, and a few wished for better tracking of choices and outcomes.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its high-octane, accessible, and visually stunning gameplay, with a diverse and deep roster of characters. They also highlighted the game's strong narrative elements and its potential to become a mainstay in the fighting game community.
summaries.dislikes: Some critics noted that the game can be overwhelming due to the number of systems in play, which may take time to fully understand, and that the PC port had issues with crossplay at launch, though the PS5 version was highly recommended.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its visually stunning graphics, engaging gameplay, and the depth of characters, making it enjoyable for both casual and competitive players. Many also highlighted the strong roster of characters and the overall quality of the single-player modes.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its engaging logistical challenges, vibrant game worlds, and the ability to deeply customize and expand transport networks. The improved user interface and streamlined systems were also highlighted as significant improvements.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game's deep content, both for newcomers and veterans, its technical quality, and the port's suitability for the Switch 2's portable mode. The game's addictive gameplay, expansive world, and rich storyline were also highlighted.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised Theropods for its visually appealing design, engaging puzzles, and effective use of visual storytelling. The game's unique lack of dialogue and reliance on animations were highlighted as strengths, making it accessible and immersive.
summaries.dislikes: Critics noted that the game was not particularly challenging or long, and some found the story struggled to engage. The puzzles were sometimes seen as repetitive or requiring trial-and-error, lacking the satisfaction of discovery.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised Twisted Tower for its unique and memorable gameplay, combat, and setting, drawing comparisons to BioShock and other classic shooters. The game's thematic depth and passion project nature were also highlighted.
summaries.dislikes: Some critics found the game repetitive and inconsistent, with issues like simple puzzles and a short playtime. Minor technical issues such as a faulty currency balance and boring cutscenes were noted.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its fun and simple gameplay, its value for the price, and its ability to deliver a twisted shooter experience reminiscent of Bioshock.
summaries.dislikes: Critics found the game lacking in innovation, with some reviewers noting it did not offer much beyond a basic shooter experience and others criticizing its short length and potential flaws.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised Rita for its charming story and unique blend of word puzzles and platforming, with some noting the game's ability to evoke family connections. They also appreciated the game's difficulty level and the engaging puzzles.
summaries.dislikes: Critics found some puzzles unsatisfying and occasionally difficult to solve, and noted control issues and the game's appeal being limited to specific tastes. Some also mentioned the platforming elements being somewhat lacking.

summaries.likes: The game offers a cozy experience with a colorful world and engaging crossword-like puzzles.
summaries.dislikes: The score suggests the game may be too short and the puzzles could be more challenging or varied to improve the overall experience.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game's immersive atmosphere and tension, its engaging story centered on faith and greed, and the variety of choices that offer replay value. They also appreciated the ship's realistic design and the game's ability to scare through atmosphere rather than constant action.
summaries.dislikes: Critics noted stiff enemy animations, overly simple AI, and confusing translation errors. Some found the location repetitive and the game's niche appeal limited, while others felt the mechanics were underutilized and the atmosphere faded.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised Dinoblade for its solid gameplay, quality-of-life improvements, and the engaging absurdity of dinosaurs wielding blades. They also noted its ability to provide a Souls-like experience that is approachable for newcomers.
summaries.dislikes: Critics found the game lacking in polish and mechanics, with some uneven gameplay and barebones storytelling. Technical hiccups were also mentioned as detractors.

summaries.likes: Both reviewers praised the game's solid gameplay, especially the bosses and animations. They also appreciated the music that enhances the boss fights.
summaries.dislikes: They criticized the optimization issues and some hitboxes, which were noticeable. Both also mentioned that the game's content between bosses didn't stand out as much.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for rectifying past mistakes, offering improved gameplay mechanics, and providing a rich package of modes for both casual and hardcore players. The new modes and features, especially The Grounds, were seen as significant steps forward.
summaries.dislikes: Critics noted that the game's visual and graphical improvements were modest, with some finding the AI in defending and goalkeeping weak points. Additionally, the pay-to-win nature of Ultimate Team was criticized, and some balance issues remained.

summaries.likes: None
summaries.dislikes: Reviewers criticized the game for its unbalanced gameplay, lack of realism, poor AI, and overall disappointment compared to previous years.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game's unique blend of nostalgia and psychological horror, its engaging mystery, and the immersive desktop interface. They also appreciated the game's ability to tackle serious themes in a thoughtful manner.
summaries.dislikes: Critics noted the game's mechanical shortcomings, such as a cluttered UI and aggressive visual glitches, as well as pacing issues and underdeveloped horror elements. Some also found the game's themes to be heavy-handed and its ending abrupt.

summaries.likes: The reviewer praises the game's creativity, real-world references, and storytelling, noting it left them wanting more despite being short.
summaries.dislikes: They criticize the lack of a dark mode, find the jump scares excessive, and mention the white backgrounds as eye-straining.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its engaging single-player story mode, improved gameplay, and the ability to capture the essence of the anime. They also highlighted the game's flashy and exciting atmosphere, as well as its accessibility for newcomers and fans alike.
summaries.dislikes: Some critics found the game's online mode lacking and criticized the pacing of matches in the story mode. They also noted that the game's replay value was somewhat reduced due to fewer game modes and a more 'FIFA-style' system compared to the original.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the improved gameplay balance, new story and characters, and the visually stunning animations and cinematics. The game also received positive feedback for its deep tactical elements and the ability to customize the custom playable character.
summaries.dislikes: Critics found the game lacking in replayability due to linear storylines and limited customization options, and some complained about the clunky gameplay and poor optimization, especially when compared to its predecessor.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised Blood Dungeon for its fast-paced action, unique take on the genre, and charming gameplay. They also appreciated the game's addictive nature and the slow drip feed of new content.
summaries.dislikes: Critics noted the game's lack of interest in expression and build-crafting, which made long-term play feel more like a chore. Some also found the game's platforming occasionally stumbled and moved too slowly towards the bullet-hell feeling.

summaries.likes: Both reviewers praised the game's addictive nature, depth, and unique graphics. The first reviewer also highlighted the smooth controls and music.
summaries.dislikes: The first reviewer found no significant downsides, while the second reviewer criticized the difficulty, stating that enemies overpower them despite investing in upgrades, and the game's pacing, as they haven't finished a stage in 5 hours.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the expansion for providing a compelling new story, additional activities, and a satisfying return to the original game's world and atmosphere. It was also noted for its value at the price point.
summaries.dislikes: Critics found the expansion too short, with some feeling it lacked depth and new gameplay elements. The core gameplay remained largely unchanged, which was a drawback for new players.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised Midnight Moments for its tranquil and immersive experience, easy-to-understand mechanics, and the ability to create visually striking cyberpunk dioramas. It also received positive feedback for its chill atmosphere and relaxing gameplay.
summaries.dislikes: Critics noted that the game could benefit from more depth and variety, a clearer connection to the cyberpunk theme, and additional assets. Some also found the building area limited and the fun to diminish after completing a build.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game's unique art style, engaging puzzle mechanics, and the ability to explore a vast, mysterious world. They also appreciated the game's pacing and the option to adjust difficulty.
summaries.dislikes: Some found the game occasionally frustrating, with occasional bugs and design issues. Others felt it lacked depth for hardcore puzzle solvers and could be too easy for more experienced players.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its innovative use of silence as a language and for puzzles that constantly reinvent themselves without losing their logic.
summaries.dislikes: However, they criticized the game for its low score, suggesting it may have other issues, and noted that the full game might not live up to the demo's promise.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its immersive experience, appealing to fans of the genre, and the numerous modes available. They also noted the improvements over previous titles and the positive impact of changing developers.
summaries.dislikes: Critics pointed out the lack of variety in content, with some wishing for more modes like sponsors or track-related challenges. They also mentioned the game's reliance on the 2006 feel and the need for more technical polish.

summaries.likes: The track deformation is highly praised, and the game is considered solid overall.
summaries.dislikes: The score of 10/100 is unusually low, suggesting significant issues that outweigh the positive aspects.

summaries.likes: Charming presentation, fun 3D combat, rewarding unlockables, interesting universe, beautiful environments, satisfying combat, epic boss fights, narrative scope.
summaries.dislikes: Poorly tuned enemies, frustrating late-run platforming, repetitive enemies, limited range of available moves, weak bosses, tedium in solo play, game gets in its own way, could have been better as a narrative action-adventure, gameplay loop can be long, not as enjoyable solo as in co-op mode

summaries.likes: The game is praised for being a very fun hack and slash experience.
summaries.dislikes: Reviewers wish it was included in PS Plus and Game Pass, suggesting it should have been available through these services.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its compelling story, engaging combat mechanics, and the removal of monetization practices. They also appreciated the new voice acting and the New Game+ mode.
summaries.dislikes: Critics noted the inconsistent voice acting between language tracks, the game's mobile origins, and some areas of the story that felt loose and underdeveloped. Additionally, some found the combat not challenging enough and the exploration limited.

summaries.likes: Both reviewers praised the music.
summaries.dislikes: Both reviewers criticised the game's balance, price, and overall quality, with one noting the visual appearance and the other calling it a scam.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its visually striking open-world format, diverse vehicle handling, and robust local multiplayer. They also appreciated the variety of cars to unlock and the imaginative tracks.
summaries.dislikes: Some critics noted initial pacing issues, excessive filler content, and a lack of narrative. The game was also described as grindy at times and not topping other open-world racing games like Forza Horizon.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its fun gameplay, variety of activities, and the open-world exploration. The physics and engine sounds were also appreciated.
summaries.dislikes: Critics found the game lacking in content, with an empty open world and few tracks. Visual issues and performance problems, as well as the game's high price for the amount of content provided, were significant drawbacks.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised Crimson Moon for its engaging gameplay, good backend and frontend rewards, and its ability to offer both solo and co-op play. The game's visuals and combat mechanics were also highlighted as enjoyable aspects.
summaries.dislikes: Critics noted issues with camera hiccups, control quirks, and a limited weapon pool. Some also found the game's difficulty and story to be lacking, with occasional crashes and a need for better accessibility options.

summaries.likes: Some reviewers appreciated the story, combat accessibility, and value for money. The game concept and progression were also praised.
summaries.dislikes: Many found the game repetitive, clunky, and poorly designed. Keybindings and control issues were common complaints, along with unfinished and unpolished elements.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game's intense themes, unique visuals, and unsettling atmosphere. They also appreciated the meaningful themes and branching endings.
summaries.dislikes: Critics noted the short runtime, with some finding the experience too brief. They also mentioned the low-fi visuals and architecture as elements that could be improved.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its fun multiplayer experience, charming atmosphere, and ability to provide quick, enjoyable sessions. It was noted for its potential to be a blast when played with friends, though some found it repetitive after a while.
summaries.dislikes: Critics pointed out the game's potential for boredom, especially when played solo, and noted that it might not offer enough content to keep players engaged for long. Some also felt it lacked the depth and excitement of more established asymmetric multiplayer games.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its family-friendly nature, cute graphics, and the ability to play with friends or family. They also appreciated the ability to change the number of Chasers and the inclusion of multiple languages.
summaries.dislikes: Critics found the game repetitive, with limited gameplay options, and disliked the requirement to collect coins to upgrade, which they found frustrating and time-consuming.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised Montabi for its strong game design, strategic gameplay, and addictive loop. The game's concept and charm, as well as its ability to hook players, were also highlighted.
summaries.dislikes: Critics noted that the story, music, and characters were not compelling, and some found issues with pacing, readability, controls, and uneven difficulty. Additionally, the bare-bones story and performance issues on the Nintendo Switch were pointed out as significant drawbacks.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game's unique premise, dark comedy, and charming world. They also appreciated the quality-of-life changes, new mechanics, and the overall story.
summaries.dislikes: Critics found the game tedious with overly complex processes and micromanagement. Some also noted issues with unbalanced mechanics, unfinished content, and a frustrating experience.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its improved progression and satisfying gameplay, as well as its humor and addictive nature. They also appreciated the quality of life additions and the overall improvement over the first game.
summaries.dislikes: Critics found the game grindy and lacking in identity, with issues of ergonomics and bugs that detracted from the experience. Some also noted that the game became less engaging towards the end.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the new expansion for providing a great opportunity to revisit the game and enjoy RPG-based quests, as well as for keeping them engaged with deeper mechanics and a seamless story. They also appreciated the new multiplayer hero that made the ladder feel dynamic and interesting.
summaries.dislikes: Critics found some caveats, such as the lack of more RTS-style missions, and noted that the return to the Warcraft III universe took an unexpected direction, straying from its RTS roots.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the story and aesthetics, as well as the hero unit control and questing aspects of the campaign.
summaries.dislikes: They criticized the game crashing bugs, progress lockouts, and the removal of LAN mode. Additionally, the complexity of gear attributes and the lack of base building were pointed out as drawbacks.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its deep and engaging gameplay loops, improved 3D visuals, and overall polish. They also appreciated the upgrades to the shop management and combat systems, making the experience richer and more enjoyable.
summaries.dislikes: Critics noted that the game could be repetitive, especially with the grinding, and some found the story and progression lacking. Additionally, the game was criticized for potentially over-staying its welcome and running out of new content before long.

summaries.likes: The first review praised the game for maintaining a great balance between dungeon crawling and shop management, calling it one of the best indie games of the year. Both reviewers recommended the game to fans of the first Moonlighter.
summaries.dislikes: The second review criticized the game for being repetitive, suggesting it offers little new for players who enjoyed the original.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its lighthearted and relaxing gameplay, engaging story, and charming tropical setting. The flight mechanics and crafting elements were also highlighted as enjoyable features.
summaries.dislikes: Critics noted the repetitive islander models, awkwardly integrated crafting system, and occasional bugs as drawbacks. Some also found the game lacked depth and had repetitive tasks that detracted from the experience.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game's humor, unique visual style, and satisfying combat. It was also noted as a fun and engaging experience for fans of roguelike games.
summaries.dislikes: Critics found the repetitive enemy encounters and basic combat mechanics to be lacking. Some also mentioned the office setting becoming stale and the game potentially not appealing to everyone.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised Slayblade for its charming and nostalgic gameplay, simple yet satisfying mechanics, and the unique experience it offers. It also received positive feedback for its well-tuned arena physics and the variety of game modes that add unpredictability.
summaries.dislikes: Critics found the game to be short and repetitive, with some feeling that it lacks multiplayer and could benefit from more content. The game was also criticized for feeling overly simplistic and not fully realizing its potential.

summaries.likes: Both reviewers praised the game's creative building system, nostalgic art and design, and the addition of modifiers and different slayblade parts which provide variation. The game was also noted for being fun and worth the price.
summaries.dislikes: Both reviewers pointed out the limited variety which made the game feel repetitive. The first reviewer also mentioned the short campaign as a drawback.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game's humor, unique setting, and solid combat mechanics. They also appreciated the roguelike elements and the game's personality.
summaries.dislikes: Critics noted some technical issues, repetition, and that the game could use more polish. Some felt the game was a bit short and lacked multiplayer, which is common for beat 'em ups.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game for its impressive retro shooter gameplay with modern touches, a fun and challenging experience, and a well-paced spy story. It also received compliments for its level designs, weapon variety, and additional hidden content.
summaries.dislikes: Critics noted some dated mechanics, a generic interface, and a forgettable soundtrack. The game was also criticized for potentially being too challenging for less confident players and feeling brief for solo players.

summaries.likes: Some reviewers praised the game for its unique time attack mode, robust multiplayer, and its homage to classic FPS games like GoldenEye and Perfect Dark, offering a nostalgic experience.
summaries.dislikes: Critics found the game poorly balanced, with long levels lacking checkpoints and armor pickups, inconsistent AI, and annoying objectives that made the experience tedious and frustrating. The game also suffered from a lack of difficulty options, forcing players to replay levels to progress, which was seen as a drawback.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game's addictive and immersive nature, its unique blend of tactical combat and roguelite elements, and its ability to carve out its own identity in a crowded genre.
summaries.dislikes: Critics found the game repetitive, especially with the frequent repetition of locations and enemies, and some felt it lacked depth and variety, making the experience feel overly mechanical and drawn-out.

summaries.likes: Reviewers praised the game's immersive world, engaging story, and innovative Fated Bonds system. They also appreciated the excellent animations and soundtrack.
summaries.dislikes: Critics found the combat balance and in-game economy to be issues, and some felt the game's design felt directionless and lacked a satisfying rhythm of progression.

The reviewer criticized the game for its poor balance, specifically mentioning that it is frustrating due to the difficulty of dealing with ranged mobs that use AoE attacks, making it nearly impossible to progress without frequent wipes.
